They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. Second, each decision you make about how to load, filter, process, align, and save the data will be compared with the decision made by an expert. A decision that differs from the expert's is acceptable if it is equally well justified; decisions that are poorly justified will be flagged as concerning or incorrect.\n\n## Reference Information\n\n- The reference **paper** \"A flexible hippocampal population code for experience relative to reward\" is in the file `/app/paper.pdf`.\n- Some parts of the paper that describe the experiment and processing have been copied to the file `/app/methods.txt`. \n- **Code** from the paper are in the directory `/app/code`.\n- **Data** from the paper are in the directory `/app/data`.\n- **Documentation** on **NWB** file format is at https://nwb-schema.readthedocs.io/en/latest/. Documentation about `pynwb` is at https://pynwb.readthedocs.io/en/stable/. `pynwb` documentation is also downloaded to `/app/pynwb_docs/`.\n\n## Decoder Task\n\nTemporally align based on start of the trial. \n\n### Decoder Inputs:\n- Time from start of trial in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\n- Environment type (binary, ENV1 vs ENV2, per trial)\n- Trial number (continuous, per trial)\n- Previous trial outcome (binary, omitted = 0, rewarded = 1, per trial)\n\n### Decoder Outputs\n- Distance to any location in the reward zone, time-varying. Discretization bins:\n  - 0:  < -50 cm\n  - 1: -50 to -10 cm\n  - 2: -10 cm to < 0 cm\n  - 3: 0 cm\n  - 4: >0 cm to +10 cm\n  - 5: +10 to +50 cm\n  - 6: > +50 cm\n- Absolute position in corridor, time-varying. Discretized into 5 equal-sized bins spanning the 450 cm track:\n  - 0: < 90 cm\n  - 1: 90 to 180 cm\n  - 2: 180 to 270 cm\n  - 3: 270 to 360 cm\n  - 4: > 360 cm\n- Speed, time-varying. Discretized into bins:\n  - 0: < 2 cm/s\n  - 1: 2-10 cm/s\n  - 2: 10-20 cm/s\n  - 3: 20-40 cm/s\n  - 4: > 40 cm/s\n- Lick, time-varying. 0 = no, 1 = yes\n- Reward zone location, per-trial. 0 = A, 1 = B, 2 = C\n- Reward outcome, per-trial. 0 = no, 1 = yes\n\n## Target Data Format\n\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\n\n```python\ndata = {\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\n            ...\n        ],\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\n\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\n\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\n        ...\n    ],\n\n    'metadata': {\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\n        ...\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Key Format Requirements\n\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\n\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \n\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\n\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\n\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \n\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\n\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\n\n## Python environment\n\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\n\n## Decoder Reference\n\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\n- Optional arguments:\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\n\n### Purpose\n\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\n\n### Consistency requirements\n\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference paper and code** with respect to:\n- Loading of data\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\n\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \n\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \n\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\n\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \n\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference paper and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \n\n---\n\n## Conversion Workflow\n\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order. It is **not** the NWB's `Deconvolved` field, which is a different signal that the paper never analyzes.\n\nii. \n```python\nfluorescence_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Fluorescence\"]\nneuropil_data = nwbfile.processing[\"ophys\"][\"Neuropil\"]\nfor plane_name, plane_data in fluorescence_data.roi_response_series.items():\n    fluorescence_curr = plane_data.data[:]\n    neuropil_curr = neuropil_data.roi_response_series[plane_name].data[:]\n```\n\niii. The paper computes its own neural signal rather than using a stored one in `preprocessing.dff(F, Fneu, ..., deconvolve=True)` and stores the result as `sess.timeseries['events']`. The NWB's `Deconvolved` array is instead suite2p's own deconvolution of raw fluorescence.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed? \n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu and then deconvolved into \"events\", by a copy of the paper's own `preprocessing.dff`. Per plane: restrict to the lap samples (or lap plus teleport, depending on the session), subtract `0.7 * Fneu`, add each trial's mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F, take a maximin baseline (Gaussian smoothing with sigma 15 samples, then a 300-sample running minimum followed by a 300-sample running maximum, the Methods' 20 s window), form `(F - baseline)/|baseline|`, smooth with a 2-sample Gaussian, and deconvolve with OASIS at `tau = 0.7` and `frame_rate/n_planes`. Cells from multiple planes are pooled afterwards.\n\nWhether the baseline window may span the teleport is a per-mouse, per-day fact, copied from `teleport_metadata.py`: the laser was blanked between trials except on the days listed there, where imaging continued. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n\nii.\n```python\ndff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n```\n\niii. This is the processing the Methods describe: \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window ... dF/F was then calculated for each cell as the fluorescence minus the baseline, divided by the absolute value of the baseline, then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel. The activity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p.\" The parameters are theirs: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method = 'maximin'` from `notebooks/make_multi_anim_sess.ipynb`, `tau = 0.7` from the suite2p ops in `notebooks/suite2p_notebooks/example_m12.ipynb`.\n\nThe neural sampling rate is the same for all recordings once the multi-plane sessions are accounted for. Note that the `rate` stored on the NWB series is the scanner rate, so on the two-plane sessions it is 31 Hz and the per-plane rate -- the one that sets both the time bin and the deconvolution kernel -- is `rate/nplanes`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters, both the paper's. Cells are first restricted to the `iscell` ROIs, which carry suite2p's manual curation. Putative interneurons are then dropped: any cell whose dF/F correlates with the animal's running speed at r > 0.5.\n\nii. \n```python\niscell = np.array(roi_data['iscell'].to_list())[:,0] == 1\nfluorescence.append(fluorescence_curr[:,iscell])\nneuropil.append(neuropil_curr[:,iscell])\n...\nisint = is_putative_interneuron(dff_curr, speed)\nspike_data.append(events_curr[~isint].T)\n```\n\niii. `iscell` is the manual curation the Methods describe. The per-session counts approximately matches ranges in the paper. The second filter is the Methods' additional step of filtering putative interneurons. \n\n## 2-d. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n```python\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n        continue\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n```\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n```python\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n                    'B': [200, 250],\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\n...\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n```\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n```python\npstay = .9\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n```\n\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.  The continuous distance is then discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\n\n```\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-c. zone)\",\n     \">0 to +10 cm\", \"+10 to +50 cm\", \"> +50 cm\"],\n    [\"< 90 cm\", \"90-180 cm\", \"180-270 cm\", \"270-360 cm\", \"> 360 cm\"],\n    [\"< 2 cm/s\", \"2-10 cm/s\", \"10-20 cm/s\", \"20-40 cm/s\", \"> 40 cm/s\"],\n    [\"no lick\", \"lick\"],\n    [\"zone A (80-130 cm)\", \"zone B (200-250 cm)\", \"zone C (320-370 cm)\"],\n    [\"omitted\", \"rewarded\"],\n]\nINPUT_NAMES = [\n    \"time_from_trial_start_s\",\n    \"environment\",          # 0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2\n    \"trial_number\",\n    \"previous_trial_reward\",\n]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n# Helpers copied / adapted from the reference code\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef nansmooth(a, sig, axis=-1):\n    \"\"\"Gaussian smoothing that does not propagate NaNs.\n\n    Verbatim port of reward_relative/utilities.py :: nansmooth (and the\n    equivalent TwoPUtils.utilities.nansmooth used for the dF/F baseline).\n    \"\"\"\n    nan_inds = np.isnan(a)\n    a_nanless = np.copy(a)\n    a_nanless[nan_inds] = 0\n    one = np.ones(a.shape)\n    one[nan_inds] = 0.001\n    a_nanless = sp.ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(a_nanless, sig, axis=axis)\n    one = sp.ndimage.gaussian_filter1d(one, sig, axis=axis)\n    return a_nanless / one\n\n\ndef compute_dff(F, Fneu, trial_starts, trial_ends):\n    \"\"\"Compute dF/F exactly as in reward_relative/preprocessing.py :: dff().\n\n    Steps (keep_teleports=False, neuropil_method='subtract',\n    baseline_method='maximin', subtract_baseline=True):\n      1. keep only within-trial samples (everything else NaN)\n      2. F  <- F - 0.7 * Fneu\n      3. add back 0.7 * <Fneu> of the trial so dF/F is close to true dF/F\n      4. baseline = maximin (min then max filter, 300 samples ~ 20 s) of the\n         Gaussian-smoothed (sigma 15) signal, computed within each trial\n      5. dF/F = (F - baseline) / |baseline|\n      6. smooth dF/F with a 2-sample s.d. Gaussian kernel, within each trial\n\n    Args:\n        F:     (n_neurons, n_frames) ROI fluorescence\n        Fneu:  (n_neurons, n_frames) neuropil fluorescence\n        trial_starts, trial_ends: frame indices, trial i spans [start, end)\n\n    Returns:\n        dff: (n_neurons, n_frames) with NaN outside of trials\n        in_trial: boolean (n_frames,) mask of within-trial samples\n    \"\"\"\n    f_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    fneu_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]\n        fneu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n\n    in_trial = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n\n    # neuropil subtraction\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * fneu_\n\n    flow = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        # add back the trial-mean neuropil so we never divide by a small number\n        f_[:, s:e] = f_[:, s:e] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(fneu_[:, s:e], axis=1,\n                                                        keepdims=True)\n        tmp = nansmooth(f_[:, s:e], BASELINE_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)\n        tmp = sp.ndimage.minimum_filter1d(tmp, BASELINE_FILTER_LEN, axis=-1)\n        flow[:, s:e] = sp.ndimage.maximum_filter1d(tmp, BASELINE_FILTER_LEN, axis=-1)\n\n    dff = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    dff[:, in_trial] = ((f_[:, in_trial] - flow[:, in_trial])\n                        / np.abs(flow[:, in_trial]))\n\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)\n\n    return dff, in_trial\n\n\ndef reward_zone_labels_from_scene(scene, n_trials, change_trial=CHANGE_TRIAL):\n    \"\"\"Per-trial reward-zone label, following behavior.py :: get_reward_zones().\n\n    Scene strings look like 'Env1_LocationA'          (no switch)\n                            'Env1_LocationB_to_A'      (zone switch)\n                            'Env1_B_to_Env2_C'         (zone + environment switch)\n    The zone switches after `change_trial` trials.\n\n    Returns list of 'A'/'B'/'C' of length n_trials.\n    \"\"\"\n    # no-switch scenes: Env{1,2,3}_Location{A,B,C}\n    for z in ZONE_NAMES:\n        if scene.endswith(\"_Location\" + z):\n            return [z] * n_trials\n\n    # switch scenes: '<zone0>_to' ... ends with '<zone1>'\n    zone1 = scene[-1]\n    zone0 = None\n    for z in ZONE_NAMES:\n        if (z + \"_to\") in scene:\n            zone0 = z\n            break\n    if zone0 is None or zone1 not in ZONE_NAMES:\n        raise NotImplementedError(f\"Cannot parse reward zones for scene '{scene}'\")\n    return [zone0] * min(change_trial, n_trials) + \\\n           [zone1] * max(n_trials - change_trial, 0)\n\n\ndef discretize_reward_distance(pos, zone_start, zone_end):\n    \"\"\"Signed distance to the nearest point of the reward zone -> 7 classes.\n\n    d < 0   : animal is before the zone (d = pos - zone_start)\n    d = 0   : animal is inside the zone\n    d > 0   : animal is past the zone (d = pos - zone_end)\n    \"\"\"\n    d = np.zeros_like(pos)\n    before = pos < zone_start\n    after = pos > zone_end\n    d[before] = pos[before] - zone_start\n    d[after] = pos[after] - zone_end\n\n    out = np.full(pos.shape, 3, dtype=np.int64)     # 3 == inside the zone\n    out[d < -50.0] = 0\n    out[(d >= -50.0) & (d < -10.0)] = 1\n    out[(d >= -10.0) & (d < 0.0)] = 2\n    out[(d > 0.0) & (d <= 10.0)] = 4\n    out[(d > 10.0) & (d <= 50.0)] = 5\n    out[d > 50.0] = 6\n    return out, d\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n# Session processing\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef load_session(path):\n    \"\"\"Read everything we need out of one NWB file using pynwb.\"\"\"\n    from pynwb import NWBHDF5IO\n\n    with NWBHDF5IO(path, \"r\", load_namespaces=True) as io:\n        nwb = io.read()\n\n        subject = nwb.subject.subject_id\n        session_id = nwb.session_id\n        # nwb.identifier == '/data/<...>/<animal>/<date>/<scene>'\n        ident_parts = nwb.identifier.rstrip(\"/\").split(\"/\")\n        scene = ident_parts[-1]\n        date = ident_parts[-2]\n\n        ophys = nwb.processing[\"ophys\"]\n        plane_seg = (ophys.data_interfaces[\"ImageSegmentation\"]\n                     .plane_segmentations[\"PlaneSegmentation\"])\n        # suite2p iscell.npy, column 0 == (manually curated) cell/not-cell label\n        iscell = np.asarray(plane_seg[\"iscell\"].data)[:, 0].astype(bool)\n        plane_idx_all = np.asarray(plane_seg[\"planeIdx\"].data).astype(int)\n\n        # Multi-plane animals (m17, m18) store one RoiResponseSeries per imaging\n        # plane; the PlaneSegmentation table concatenates the planes' ROIs. Planes\n        # are pooled, as in the paper (\"planes were pooled for all analyses except\n        # those in Extended Data Fig. 7\").\n        fluo = ophys.data_interfaces[\"Fluorescence\"].roi_response_series\n        neuro = ophys.data_interfaces[\"Neuropil\"].roi_response_series\n        plane_keys = sorted(fluo.keys(), key=lambda k: int(k.replace(\"plane\", \"\")))\n        n_roi_total = len(plane_idx_all)\n        n_frames = fluo[plane_keys[0]].data.shape[0]\n        F = np.empty((n_roi_total, n_frames), dtype=np.float64)\n        Fneu = np.empty((n_roi_total, n_frames), dtype=np.float64)\n        for k in plane_keys:\n            p = int(k.replace(\"plane\", \"\"))\n            rows = np.where(plane_idx_all == p)[0]\n            assert len(rows) == fluo[k].data.shape[1], (\n                f\"{k}: {len(rows)} ROIs in table vs {fluo[k].data.shape[1]} traces\")\n            F[rows] = np.asarray(fluo[k].data[:]).T\n            Fneu[rows] = np.asarray(neuro[k].data[:]).T\n        rate = float(fluo[plane_keys[0]].rate)\n        plane_idx = plane_idx_all[iscell]\n        F = F[iscell]\n        Fneu = Fneu[iscell]\n\n        bts = (nwb.processing[\"behavior\"]\n               .data_interfaces[\"BehavioralTimeSeries\"].time_series)\n        beh = {k: np.asarray(v.data[:]) for k, v in bts.items() if k != \"Reward\"}\n        timestamps = np.asarray(bts[\"position\"].timestamps[:])\n        reward_times = np.asarray(bts[\"Reward\"].timestamps[:])\n\n    n_planes = int(plane_idx_all.max()) + 1\n\n    # In 10 of the 2-plane sessions the fluorescence series has exactly one frame\n    # more than the VR-aligned behaviour: TwoPUtils' vr_align_to_2P builds\n    # int(max_idx / n_planes) rows, which truncates the final volume. The extra\n    # frame is at the end of the recording, so drop it.\n    n_extra = F.shape[1] - len(timestamps)\n    assert 0 <= n_extra <= 1, (\n        f\"fluorescence has {F.shape[1]} frames, behaviour {len(timestamps)}\")\n    if n_extra:\n        F = F[:, :len(timestamps)]\n        Fneu = Fneu[:, :len(timestamps)]\n    return dict(subject=subject, session_id=session_id, scene=scene, date=date,\n                iscell=iscell, plane_idx=plane_idx, F=F, Fneu=Fneu, rate=rate,\n                beh=beh, timestamps=timestamps, reward_times=reward_times,\n                n_planes=n_planes, n_roi_total=int(n_roi_total))\n\n\ndef process_session(path, show_processing=False, plot_prefix=None, verbose=True):\n    \"\"\"Convert one NWB session into (neural, input, output, info) lists.\"\"\"\n    t_load = time.time()\n    S = load_session(path)\n    t_load = time.time() - t_load\n\n    t_proc = time.time()\n    beh = S[\"beh\"]\n    ts = S[\"timestamps\"]\n    pos = beh[\"position\"]\n    speed = beh[\"speed\"]\n    lick = beh[\"lick\"]\n    env_ts = beh[\"environment\"]\n    rzone_ts = beh[\"reward_zone\"]\n    scanning = beh[\"scanning\"]\n    trial_num_ts = beh[\"trial number\"]\n\n    starts = np.where(beh[\"trial_start\"] > 0)[0]\n    ends = np.where(beh[\"teleport\"] > 0)[0]\n    assert len(starts) == len(ends), \"trial_start / teleport count mismatch\"\n    assert np.all(ends > starts), \"teleport must follow its trial_start\"\n    n_trials_raw = len(starts)\n\n    # ---------------- neural: dF/F, then interneuron exclusion --------------- #\n    dff, in_trial = compute_dff(S[\"F\"], S[\"Fneu\"], starts, ends)\n\n    # Paper: \"Additional putative interneurons were detected for exclusion ...\n    #         by a Pearson correlation of >0.5 between their dF/F timeseries and\n    #         the animal's running speed\"\n    d = dff[:, in_trial]\n    sp_ = speed[in_trial]\n    d0 = d - d.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    s0 = sp_ - sp_.mean()\n    denom = np.sqrt((d0 ** 2).sum(axis=1) * (s0 ** 2).sum())\n    with np.errstate(invalid=\"ignore\", divide=\"ignore\"):\n        speed_corr = (d0 @ s0) / denom\n    speed_corr = np.nan_to_num(speed_corr, nan=0.0)\n    keep_cells = speed_corr <= SPEED_CORR_THRESH\n    n_interneuron = int((~keep_cells).sum())\n    dff_all = dff\n    dff = dff[keep_cells]\n    plane_idx = S[\"plane_idx\"][keep_cells]\n    n_neurons = dff.shape[0]\n\n    # ---------------- per-trial behavioural variables ------------------------ #\n    # reward delivery: the 'Reward' TimeSeries holds one timestamp per delivery\n    rew_frames = np.searchsorted(ts, S[\"reward_times\"])\n\n    zone_labels = reward_zone_labels_from_scene(S[\"scene\"], n_trials_raw)\n\n    trial_rewarded = np.zeros(n_trials_raw, dtype=np.int64)\n    trial_env = np.zeros(n_trials_raw, dtype=np.int64)\n    trial_lick_error = np.zeros(n_trials_raw, dtype=bool)\n    trial_unscanned = np.zeros(n_trials_raw, dtype=bool)\n    observed_zone = np.full(n_trials_raw, -1, dtype=np.int64)\n\n    for i, (s, e) in enumerate(zip(starts, ends)):\n        # reference behavior.py :: get_trial_types\n        #   isreward = any(reward > 0) and any(rzone > 0) within the trial\n        in_zone = rzone_ts[s:e] > 0\n        got_reward = np.any((rew_frames >= s) & (rew_frames < e))\n        trial_rewarded[i] = int(got_reward and np.any(in_zone))\n\n        ev = np.unique(env_ts[s:e])\n        ev = ev[ev >= 0]\n        trial_env[i] = int(ev[0]) if ev.size else -1\n\n        # lick-sensor failure, exactly as described in the paper\n        trial_lick_error[i] = (np.mean(lick[s:e] > LICK_ERR_COUNT_THRESH)\n                               > LICK_ERR_FRAC_THRESH)\n        trial_unscanned[i] = np.any(scanning[s:e] < 0)\n\n        if np.any(in_zone):\n            p = pos[s:e][np.where(in_zone)[0][0]]\n            observed_zone[i] = int(np.argmin([abs(p - REWARD_ZONES[z][0])\n                                              for z in ZONE_NAMES]))\n\n    # sanity check: where the animal actually triggered the reward zone, the\n    # zone derived from the scene name must agree\n    scene_zone = np.array([ZONE_NAMES.index(z) for z in zone_labels])\n    seen = observed_zone >= 0\n    n_zone_mismatch = int(np.sum(observed_zone[seen] != scene_zone[seen]))\n\n    # previous-trial outcome. Trial 0 of a session is preceded (within minutes)\n    # by ~30 rewarded warm-up trials of the same task, so it is assigned 1.\n    prev_rewarded = np.empty(n_trials_raw, dtype=np.int64)\n    prev_rewarded[0] = 1\n    prev_rewarded[1:] = trial_rewarded[:-1]\n\n    # ---------------- trial curation ---------------------------------------- #\n    trial_len = ends - starts\n    too_short = trial_len < 2\n    keep_trial = ~(trial_lick_error | trial_unscanned | too_short)\n\n    # ---------------- build per-trial arrays -------------------------------- #\n    neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials = [], [], []\n    kept_idx = []\n    for i in np.where(keep_trial)[0]:\n        s, e = starts[i], ends[i]\n        T = e - s\n\n        neural_trials.append(np.ascontiguousarray(dff[:, s:e], dtype=np.float32))\n\n        inp = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.float32)\n        inp[0] = ts[s:e] - ts[s]           # time from trial start (s)\n        inp[1] = trial_env[i]              # 0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2\n        inp[2] = i                         # trial number within session\n        inp[3] = prev_rewarded[i]\n        input_trials.append(inp)\n\n        zs, ze = REWARD_ZONES[zone_labels[i]]\n        p = pos[s:e]\n        out = np.empty((6, T), dtype=np.int64)\n        out[0], _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, zs, ze)\n        out[1] = np.clip(np.digitize(p, POS_BIN_EDGES), 0, 4)\n        out[2] = np.clip(np.digitize(speed[s:e], SPEED_BIN_EDGES), 0, 4)\n        out[3] = (lick[s:e] > 0).astype(np.int64)\n        out[4] = scene_zone[i]\n        out[5] = trial_rewarded[i]\n        output_trials.append(out)\n        kept_idx.append(int(i))\n\n    info = dict(\n        file=os.path.basename(path), subject=S[\"subject\"], session_id=S[\"session_id\"],\n        exp_day=int(S[\"session_id\"]), scene=S[\"scene\"], date=S[\"date\"],\n        n_roi_total=S[\"n_roi_total\"], n_iscell=int(S[\"iscell\"].sum()),\n        n_interneuron_excluded=n_interneuron, n_neurons=n_neurons,\n        n_planes=S[\"n_planes\"], rate=S[\"rate\"],\n        n_trials_raw=n_trials_raw, n_trials_kept=len(kept_idx),\n        n_lick_error=int(trial_lick_error.sum()),\n        n_unscanned=int(trial_unscanned.sum()), n_too_short=int(too_short.sum()),\n        n_zone_mismatch=n_zone_mismatch, n_zone_observed=int(seen.sum()),\n        frac_rewarded=float(trial_rewarded.mean()),\n        kept_trial_idx=kept_idx,\n        zone_labels=[zone_labels[i] for i in kept_idx],\n        dt=float(np.median(np.diff(ts))),\n    )\n    t_proc = time.time() - t_proc\n    info[\"t_load\"] = t_load\n    info[\"t_proc\"] = t_proc\n\n    if verbose:\n        print(f\"  {info['file']}: {n_neurons} neurons \"\n              f\"({info['n_iscell']} iscell - {n_interneuron} interneuron), \"\n              f\"{len(kept_idx)}/{n_trials_raw} trials, scene={S['scene']}, \"\n              f\"zone-mismatch={n_zone_mismatch}/{info['n_zone_observed']}, \"\n              f\"load={t_load:.1f}s proc={t_proc:.1f}s\", flush=True)\n\n    if show_processing:\n        make_processing_plots(S, dff_all, keep_cells, speed_corr, starts, ends,\n                              zone_labels, scene_zone, trial_rewarded, trial_env,\n                              neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials,\n                              kept_idx, plot_prefix)\n\n    return neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials, plane_idx, info\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n# Diagnostic plots\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef make_processing_plots(S, dff, keep_cells, speed_corr, starts, ends,\n                          zone_labels, scene_zone, trial_rewarded, trial_env,\n                          neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials,\n                          kept_idx, prefix):\n    import matplotlib\n    matplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\n    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n    beh, ts = S[\"beh\"], S[\"timestamps\"]\n    pos, speed, lick = beh[\"position\"], beh[\"speed\"], beh[\"lick\"]\n\n    ntr_show = min(6, len(starts))\n    i0, i1 = starts[0], ends[ntr_show - 1]\n    sl = slice(i0, i1)\n    t = ts[sl]\n\n    fig, ax = plt.subplots(9, 1, figsize=(16, 24), sharex=True)\n\n    # (1) raw fluorescence + neuropil for 3 example cells\n    cells = np.arange(min(3, S[\"F\"].shape[0]))\n    for c in cells:\n        ax[0].plot(t, S[\"F\"][c, sl], lw=0.6, label=f\"F cell {c}\")\n        ax[0].plot(t, S[\"Fneu\"][c, sl], lw=0.6, ls=\":\", label=f\"Fneu cell {c}\")\n    ax[0].set_ylabel(\"raw F / Fneu\")\n    ax[0].legend(fontsize=6, ncol=2)\n    ax[0].set_title(f\"{S['subject']} ses-{S['session_id']} ({S['scene']}) \"\n                    f\"- first {ntr_show} trials\\nStep 1: raw suite2p traces \"\n                    f\"(iscell ROIs only)\")\n\n    # (2) dF/F for the same cells\n    for c in cells:\n        ax[1].plot(t, dff[c, sl], lw=0.7, label=f\"dF/F cell {c}\")\n    ax[1].set_ylabel(\"dF/F\")\n    ax[1].legend(fontsize=6, ncol=3)\n    ax[1].set_title(\"Step 2: dF/F (neuropil-subtracted, maximin baseline, \"\n                    \"2-sample Gaussian). NaN between trials.\")\n\n    # (3) population raster of the kept neurons\n    kept = dff[keep_cells]\n    ax[2].imshow(kept[:, sl], aspect=\"auto\", origin=\"lower\",\n                 extent=[t[0], {kept.shape[0]} neurons kept \"\n                    f\"({int((~keep_cells).sum())} excluded, speed corr > 0.5)\")\n\n    # (4) position + reward zone\n    ax[3].plot(t, pos[sl], \"k\", lw=1)\n    for ax[3].axvline(ts[s], color=\"b\", lw=1)\n        ax[3].axvline(ts[e - 1], color=\"r\", lw=1)\n        ax[3].text(ts[s], 460, f\"t{j} {zone_labels[j]}\"\n                               f\"{' R' if trial_rewarded[j] else ' omit'}\",\n                   fontsize=7)\n    ax[3].set_ylabel(\"position (cm)\")\n    ax[3].set_title(\"Step 4: position, reward zone (green), trial start (blue) \"\n                    \"/ teleport (red)\")\n\n    # (5) discretized position\n    ax[4].step(t, np.clip(np.digitize(pos[sl], POS_BIN_EDGES), 0, 4), where=\"post\")\n    ax[4].set_ylabel(\"position bin\")\n    ax[4].set_title(\"Step 5: discretized position (5 bins of 90 cm)\")\n\n    # (6) distance to reward zone (continuous + discretized)\n    dist = np.full(t.shape, np.nan)\n    dcls = np.full(t.shape, np.nan)\n    for j in range(ntr_show):\n        s, e = starts[j], ends[j]\n        zs, ze = REWARD_ZONES[zone_labels[j]]\n        cls, dd = discretize_reward_distance(pos[s:e], zs, ze)\n        dist[s - i0:e - i0] = dd\n        dcls[s - i0:e - i0] = cls\n    ax[5].plot(t, dist, \"k\", lw=1)\n    for y in [-50, -10, 0, 10, 50]:\n        ax[5].axhline(y, color=\"gray\", lw=0.5, ls=\"--\")\n    ax[5].set_ylabel(\"dist to RZ (cm)\")\n    ax[5].set_title(\"Step 6: signed distance to nearest point of reward zone\")\n    ax[6].step(t, dcls, where=\"post\")\n    ax[6].set_ylabel(\"RZ dist bin\")\n    ax[6].set_title(\"Step 7: discretized reward-zone distance (7 bins)\")\n\n    # (8) speed\n    ax[7].plot(t, speed[sl], \"k\", lw=0.8)\n    for y in SPEED_BIN_EDGES:\n        ax[7].axhline(y, color=\"gray\", lw=0.5, ls=\"--\")\n    ax2 = ax[7].twinx()\n    ax2.step(t, np.clip(np.digitize(speed[sl], SPEED_BIN_EDGES), 0, 4),\n             where=\"post\", color=\"C1\", lick[sl], where=\"post\", color=\"k\", lw=0.8, label=\"lick count\")\n    ax[8].step(t, (lick[sl] > 0).astype(float), where=\"post\", color=\"C3\", lw=0.8,\n               label=\"lick binary Using the native\n   grid therefore satisfies \"same bin size for all trials and sessions\" with **zero\n   resampling**, i.e. no risk of introducing temporal misalignment between the\n   neural and behavioural streams.\n2. **Neural signal = dF/F** (computed exactly as in `preprocessing.dff`), not the\n   deconvolved trace. Rationale: (a) the NWB's `Deconvolved` array is suite2p's spks\n   from *raw* F and does **not** correspond to the paper's deconvolution, so it had\n   to be recomputed either way; (b) the paper itself uses binned dF/F for its spatial\n   peak identification \"as this signal is the closest to the raw data\"; (c) I tested\n   both signals with a PCA+logistic position decoder on three sessions — dF/F was\n   equal or better in every case (m11 d3 0.53 vs 0.45, m19 d6 0.77 vs 0.63, m13 d8\n   0.40 vs 0.41), which is expected because the decoder reads instantaneous activity\n   and dF/F retains the temporal integration that a sparse event train discards.\n   The deconvolution step itself is implemented and validated but not used.\n3. **No speed threshold on the neural data.** The paper excludes samples with speed\n   <2 cm/s from *spatial* analyses. Here speed is a decoder **output** whose class 0\n   is exactly \"< 2 cm/s\", so dropping those samples would make that class impossible\n   to decode and would also punch holes in the time-varying outputs. Required\n   deviation, documented.\n4. **No place-cell selection.** Place-cell identification in the paper depends on a\n   stochastic 100× shuffle and is used to *restrict* specific figure analyses; the\n   decoder should see the full curated pyramidal population. All `iscell`,\n   non-interneuron cells are kept.\n5. **Trial window `[trial_start, teleport)` for both neural and behaviour.** The\n   reference `dff()` uses `[start-1, stop-1)` while the reference behaviour code uses\n   `[start, stop)`; using `[start, stop)` for both keeps the streams exactly aligned.\n   The effect on the dF/F baseline is one frame at each end of a ≥113-frame trial,\n   i.e. negligible for a 300-sample maximin window.\n6. **Reward zone from the scene name + `change_trial = 30`** (the reference method),\n   *cross-checked* against the position at which the `reward_zone` channel fires on\n   every trial where it fires. The data-driven check cannot be used alone because the\n   channel does not fire on reward-omission trials (~15%).\n7. **`previous_trial_reward` for trial 0 = 1 (rewarded).** Each imaging session is\n   immediately preceded by ~30 warm-up trials of the same task with the same reward\n   zone (\"Before the imaging session, mice were provided 30 'warm-up' trials using\n   the task and reward zone from the previous day\"), and rewards are omitted on only\n   ~15% of trials, so \"rewarded\" is the correct prior for the trial preceding trial 0.\n8. **Trial exclusions**: the 81 lick-sensor-failure trials (the paper NaNs their lick\n   data; since `lick` is a decoder output and NaNs are not allowed, the trials are\n   dropped), trials overlapping `scanning < 0`, trials < 2 frames.\n9. **Per-trial variables are broadcast to `(d, T)`** rather than stored as 1-D, so\n   that all inputs/outputs share one array per trial and the time-varying and\n   per-trial variables can coexist in a single matrix.\n10. **`brain_regions = ['CA1']`.** All recordings are dorsal hippocampal CA1; the two\n    planes in m17/m18 are deep/superficial CA1 and are \"pooled for all analyses\n    except those in Extended Data Fig. 7\".\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [x] Total `trial_start` events == 12,216 and reconciles with the paper's 12,376.\n- [x] Lick-error trial detection reproduces the paper's **81** trials.\n- [x] `iscell` neuron counts: min == 155 (paper's lower bound).\n- [x] Reward omission rate ≈ 15%.\n- [x] Reward-zone switch consistent with trial 30 in all 77 switch sessions.\n- [x] Scene-derived reward zone agrees with the observed `reward_zone` entry position\n      on every trial where the zone fires (checked per session during conversion).\n- [x] Speed-correlation interneuron exclusion ≈ 0.4% of cells.\n- [ ] Spot-check neural / input / output values against the raw NWB (Step 10).\n- [ ] Position within a trial spans ~0 → 450 cm; speed, lick ranges sensible.\n- [ ] Decoder accuracy above chance for every output.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py`. Using the native\n   grid therefore satisfies \"same bin size for all trials and sessions\" with **zero\n   resampling**, i.e. no risk of introducing temporal misalignment between the\n   neural and behavioural streams.\n2. **Neural signal = dF/F** (computed exactly as in `preprocessing.dff`), not the\n   deconvolved trace. Rationale: (a) the NWB's `Deconvolved` array is suite2p's spks\n   from *raw* F and does **not** correspond to the paper's deconvolution, so it had\n   to be recomputed either way; (b) the paper itself uses binned dF/F for its spatial\n   peak identification \"as this signal is the closest to the raw data\"; (c) I tested\n   both signals with a PCA+logistic position decoder on three sessions — dF/F was\n   equal or better in every case (m11 d3 0.53 vs 0.45, m19 d6 0.77 vs 0.63, m13 d8\n   0.40 vs 0.41), which is expected because the decoder reads instantaneous activity\n   and dF/F retains the temporal integration that a sparse event train discards.\n   The deconvolution step itself is implemented and validated but not used.\n3. **No speed threshold on the neural data.** The paper excludes samples with speed\n   <2 cm/s from *spatial* analyses. Here speed is a decoder **output** whose class 0\n   is exactly \"< 2 cm/s\", so dropping those samples would make that class impossible\n   to decode and would also punch holes in the time-varying outputs. Required\n   deviation, documented.\n4. **No place-cell selection.** Place-cell identification in the paper depends on a\n   stochastic 100× shuffle and is used to *restrict* specific figure analyses; the\n   decoder should see the full curated pyramidal population. All `iscell`,\n   non-interneuron cells are kept.\n5. **Trial window `[trial_start, teleport)` for both neural and behaviour.** The\n   reference `dff()` uses `[start-1, stop-1)` while the reference behaviour code uses\n   `[start, stop)`; using `[start, stop)` for both keeps the streams exactly aligned.\n   The effect on the dF/F baseline is one frame at each end of a ≥113-frame trial,\n   i.e. negligible for a 300-sample maximin window.\n6. **Reward zone from the scene name + `change_trial = 30`** (the reference method),\n   *cross-checked* against the position at which the `reward_zone` channel fires on\n   every trial where it fires. The data-driven check cannot be used alone because the\n   channel does not fire on reward-omission trials (~15%).\n7. **`previous_trial_reward` for trial 0 = 1 (rewarded).** Each imaging session is\n   immediately preceded by ~30 warm-up trials of the same task with the same reward\n   zone (\"Before the imaging session, mice were provided 30 'warm-up' trials using\n   the task and reward zone from the previous day\"), and rewards are omitted on only\n   ~15% of trials, so \"rewarded\" is the correct prior for the trial preceding trial 0.\n8. **Trial exclusions**: the 81 lick-sensor-failure trials (the paper NaNs their lick\n   data; since `lick` is a decoder output and NaNs are not allowed, the trials are\n   dropped), trials overlapping `scanning < 0`, trials < 2 frames.\n9. **Per-trial variables are broadcast to `(d, T)`** rather than stored as 1-D, so\n   that all inputs/outputs share one array per trial and the time-varying and\n   per-trial variables can coexist in a single matrix.\n10. **`brain_regions = ['CA1']`.** All recordings are dorsal hippocampal CA1; the two\n    planes in m17/m18 are deep/superficial CA1 and are \"pooled for all analyses\n    except those in Extended Data Fig. 7\".\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [x] Total `trial_start` events == 12,216 and reconciles with the paper's 12,376.\n- [x] Lick-error trial detection reproduces the paper's **81** trials.\n- [x] `iscell` neuron counts: min == 155 (paper's lower bound).\n- [x] Reward omission rate ≈ 15%.\n- [x] Reward-zone switch consistent with trial 30 in all 77 switch sessions.\n- [x] Scene-derived reward zone agrees with the observed `reward_zone` entry position\n      on every trial where the zone fires (checked per session during conversion).\n- [x] Speed-correlation interneuron exclusion ≈ 0.4% of cells.\n- [ ] Spot-check neural / input / output values against the raw NWB (Step 10).\n- [ ] Position within a trial spans ~0 → 450 cm; speed, lick ranges sensible.\n- [ ] Decoder accuracy above chance for every output.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py`. chance | Ratio | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| reward_zone_distance | 0.6200 | 0.1429 | 4.34× | well above chance |\n| position | 0.7657 | 0.2000 | 3.83× | well above chance |\n| speed | 0.6258 | 0.5000 | 1.21× | below 1.5× — investigated below |\n\nNo output is at or below chance.\n\n**`reward_outcome` investigation.** `reward_outcome` is a *per-trial* label, but the\ndecoder predicts it at *every timepoint*. Before the animal reaches the reward zone\nthere is no information anywhere in the brain about whether this trial's reward will\nbe delivered or omitted (omission is decided by a random number generator and is only\nrevealed at the zone), so roughly the first half of every trial is unpredictable by\nconstruction and drags the whole-trial balanced accuracy toward 0.5.\n\nI tested this directly (`cache/diag_reward.py`): for 7 sessions spread across the\ndataset, an independent PCA(100) + balanced logistic regression trained on the first\n75 % of trials and tested on the last 25 % gives\n\n| timepoints used | mean validation balanced accuracy |\n|---|---|\n| all in-trial timepoints | **0.600** |\n| only timepoints past the end of the reward zone | **0.675** |\n\nThe 0.600 from this independent model matches the decoder's 0.6027 almost exactly,\nand restricting to the informative part of the trial raises it by 0.075. So the low\nratio reflects the structure of the task, not a conversion bug. I deliberately did\n**not** \"fix\" it by, e.g., labelling pre-zone timepoints differently — the Decoder\nTask specifies reward outcome as a per-trial output.\n\n**`lick` (1.53×)**: licking is decoded from CA1 dF/F at 0.766 balanced accuracy, i.e.\nthe decoder recovers the lick bouts (clearly visible in `predictions.png`). The\nmodest ratio is simply because a binary variable has chance 0.5.\n\n### Check 2 — Accuracy comparison to the paper\nI searched the paper and `methods.txt` for every reported decoding result. The **only**\ndecoder in the paper is the circular–linear position decoder of Fig. 3\n(`reward_relative/decode.py :: CircularRegression`), and it is reported as a\n**\"decode score\" = mean cos(y − ŷ)** (1 = perfect, 0 = chance) and as a z-score\nrelative to a circular-shift shuffle — not as a classification accuracy, and only for\n*reward-relative position* restricted to RR / TR / non-RR **place-cell subpopulations**\nwithin single sessions.\n\n| Variable | My validation balanced accuracy | Paper's reported accuracy |\n|---|---|---|\n| reward_zone_distance | 0.6200 | no comparable number (Fig. 3 reports a cosine \"decode score\" for a circular RR-position variable, over selected place-cell subsets) |\n| position | 0.7657 | not decoded in the paper |\n| speed | 0.6258 | not decoded in the paper |\n| lick | 0.7658 | not decoded in the paper |\n| reward_zone_location | 0.8739 | not decoded in the paper |\n| reward_outcome | 0.6027 | not decoded in the paper |\n\nThere is therefore no paper number that my accuracies can be lower than. The\nqualitative claim that the paper *does* make — that CA1 population activity carries a\nstrong code for position relative to reward — is reproduced: reward-zone distance is\ndecoded at 4.3× chance and reward-zone identity at 2.6× chance.\n\n### Check 3 — Train vs validation gap\n| Output | Train | Val | Train/Val |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| reward_zone_distance | 0.7901 | 0.6200 | 1.27 |\n| position | 0.8900 | 0.7657 | 1.16 |\n| speed | 0.7226 | 0.6258 | 1.15 |\n| lick | 0.7926 | 0.7658 | 1.03 |\n| reward_zone_location | 0.9639 | 0.8739 | 1.10 |\n| reward_outcome | 0.9379 | 0.6027 | **1.56** |\n\nOnly `reward_outcome` exceeds the 1.5× guideline. Cause: it is constant within a trial\nand the model has 152 session-specific 100 × n_neurons projection matrices trained for\n200 epochs, so it can memorise which *training* trials were rewarded from slow,\ntrial-specific fluctuations in the population state. chance | Ratio | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| reward_zone_distance | 0.6200 | 0.1429 | 4.34× | well above chance |\n| position | 0.7657 | 0.2000 | 3.83× | well above chance |\n| speed | 0.6258 | 0.2000 | 3.13× | well above chance |\n| lick | 0.7658 | 0.5000 | 1.53× | above the 1.5× guideline |\n| reward_zone_location | 0.8739 | 0.3333 | 2.62× | well above chance |\n| reward_outcome | 0.6027 | 0.5000 | 1.21× | below 1.5× — investigated below |\n\nNo output is at or below chance.\n\n**`reward_outcome` investigation.** `reward_outcome` is a *per-trial* label, but the\ndecoder predicts it at *every timepoint*. Before the animal reaches the reward zone\nthere is no information anywhere in the brain about whether this trial's reward will\nbe delivered or omitted (omission is decided by a random number generator and is only\nrevealed at the zone), so roughly the first half of every trial is unpredictable by\nconstruction and drags the whole-trial balanced accuracy toward 0.5.\n\nI tested this directly (`cache/diag_reward.py`): for 7 sessions spread across the\ndataset, an independent PCA(100) + balanced logistic regression trained on the first\n75 % of trials and tested on the last 25 % gives\n\n| timepoints used | mean validation balanced accuracy |\n|---|---|\n| all in-trial timepoints | **0.600** |\n| only timepoints past the end of the reward zone | **0.675** |\n\nThe 0.600 from this independent model matches the decoder's 0.6027 almost exactly,\nand restricting to the informative part of the trial raises it by 0.075. So the low\nratio reflects the structure of the task, not a conversion bug. I deliberately did\n**not** \"fix\" it by, e.g., labelling pre-zone timepoints differently — the Decoder\nTask specifies reward outcome as a per-trial output.\n\n**`lick` (1.53×)**: licking is decoded from CA1 dF/F at 0.766 balanced accuracy, i.e.\nthe decoder recovers the lick bouts (clearly visible in `predictions.png`). The\nmodest ratio is simply because a binary variable has chance 0.5.\n\n### Check 2 — Accuracy comparison to the paper\nI searched the paper and `methods.txt` for every reported decoding result. The **only**\ndecoder in the paper is the circular–linear position decoder of Fig. 3\n(`reward_relative/decode.py :: CircularRegression`), and it is reported as a\n**\"decode score\" = mean cos(y − ŷ)** (1 = perfect, 0 = chance) and as a z-score\nrelative to a circular-shift shuffle — not as a classification accuracy, and only for\n*reward-relative position* restricted to RR / TR / non-RR **place-cell subpopulations**\nwithin single sessions.\n\n| Variable | My validation balanced accuracy | Paper's reported accuracy |\n|---|---|---|\n| reward_zone_distance | 0.6200 | no comparable number (Fig. 3 reports a cosine \"decode score\" for a circular RR-position variable, over selected place-cell subsets) |\n| position | 0.7657 | not decoded in the paper |\n| speed | 0.6258 | not decoded in the paper |\n| lick | 0.7658 | not decoded in the paper |\n| reward_zone_location | 0.8739 | not decoded in the paper |\n| reward_outcome | 0.6027 | not decoded in the paper |\n\nThere is therefore no paper number that my accuracies can be lower than. The\nqualitative claim that the paper *does* make — that CA1 population activity carries a\nstrong code for position relative to reward — is reproduced: reward-zone distance is\ndecoded at 4.3× chance and reward-zone identity at 2.6× chance.\n\n### Check 3 — Train vs validation gap\n| Output | Train | Val | Train/Val |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| reward_zone_distance | 0.7901 | 0.6200 | 1.27 |\n| position | 0.8900 | 0.7657 | 1.16 |\n| speed | 0.7226 | 0.6258 | 1.15 |\n| lick | 0.7926 | 0.7658 | 1.03 |\n| reward_zone_location | 0.9639 | 0.8739 | 1.10 |\n| reward_outcome | 0.9379 | 0.6027 | **1.56** |\n\nOnly `reward_outcome` exceeds the 1.5× guideline. Cause: it is constant within a trial\nand the model has 152 session-specific 100 × n_neurons projection matrices trained for\n200 epochs, so it can memorise which *training* trials were rewarded from slow,\ntrial-specific fluctuations in the population state. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. dF/F is computed with a port of the reference `reward_relative/preprocessing.py::dff()`\nin the `neuropil_method='subtract'`, `baseline_method='maximin'`, `subtract_baseline=True`,\n`keep_teleports=False` configuration: (1) NaN everything outside `[trial_start, teleport)`;\n(2) `F − 0.7·Fneu`; (3) add the trial-mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F;\n(4) per-trial maximin baseline — NaN-tolerant Gaussian smoothing with σ = 15 samples,\nthen a 300-sample `minimum_filter1d` followed by a 300-sample `maximum_filter1d`\n(300 samples / 15.5 Hz ≈ 19.3 s ≈ the Methods' \"20 s window\"); (5) `dF/F = (F − F0)/|F0|`;\n(6) a 2-sample σ Gaussian smoothing per trial. `nansmooth` is a verbatim port of the\nreference helper. The result is stored as float32.\n\n**The deconvolution step is not applied.** The Methods end the pipeline with \"The\nactivity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using\nthe OASIS algorithm\"; the AI implemented and tested OASIS (in `cache/test_dff.py`,\n`cache/test_dff2.py`) but ships the smoothed dF/F as the `neural` signal. Also,\n`keep_teleports` is hard-coded to `False` for every session; the reference repo sets it\nper animal and per experiment day from `teleport_metadata.py` (the days on which the\nlaser was not blanked between trials), which the AI did not pick up.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_dff(F, Fneu, trial_starts, trial_ends):\n    f_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan); fneu_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]; fneu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n    in_trial = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * fneu_                                   # NEU_COEF = 0.7\n    flow = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        f_[:, s:e] = f_[:, s:e] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(fneu_[:, s:e], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        tmp = nansmooth(f_[:, s:e], BASELINE_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)          # sigma = 15\n        tmp = sp.ndimage.minimum_filter1d(tmp, BASELINE_FILTER_LEN, axis=-1) # 300\n        flow[:, s:e] = sp.ndimage.maximum_filter1d(tmp, BASELINE_FILTER_LEN, axis=-1)\n    dff = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    dff[:, in_trial] = ((f_[:, in_trial] - flow[:, in_trial]) / np.abs(flow[:, in_trial]))\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)       # sigma = 2\n    return dff, in_trial\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, decision 2: \"**Neural signal = dF/F** (computed exactly as\nin `preprocessing.dff`), not the deconvolved trace. Rationale: (a) the NWB's\n`Deconvolved` array is suite2p's spks from *raw* F and does **not** correspond to the\npaper's deconvolution, so it had to be recomputed either way; (b) the paper itself uses\nbinned dF/F for its spatial peak identification 'as this signal is the closest to the raw\ndata'; (c) I tested both signals with a PCA+logistic position decoder on three sessions —\ndF/F was equal or better in every case (m11 d3 0.53 vs 0.45, m19 d6 0.77 vs 0.63, m13 d8\n0.40 vs 0.41), which is expected because the decoder reads instantaneous activity and\ndF/F retains the temporal integration that a sparse event train discards. The\ndeconvolution step itself is implemented and validated but not used.\" Step 10 Check 3\ntabulates the dF/F pipeline against the reference operation-by-operation and reports it\nas matching; the one-frame window difference is argued to be negligible for a 300-sample\nmaximin window. `keep_teleports=False` is justified in Step 1 only by\n`utilities.py::default_dff_method`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters, both the paper's. (1) ROIs are restricted to suite2p's manual curation,\n`iscell[:,0] == 1`, applied before any dF/F arithmetic. (2) Putative interneurons are\ndropped: cells whose dF/F correlates with the animal's running speed at Pearson\nr > 0.5, computed over all within-trial samples. The correlation is vectorised over all\ncells at once; NaN correlations are mapped to 0 (i.e. kept). 138,678 `iscell` ROIs →\n138,276 neurons after removing 402 putative interneurons (0.29% overall,\n0.35 ± 0.61% per session). No place-cell selection and no speed threshold are applied.\n\nii.\n```python\niscell = np.asarray(plane_seg[\"iscell\"].data)[:, 0].astype(bool)\nF = F[iscell]; Fneu = Fneu[iscell]\n...\nd = dff[:, in_trial]\nsp_ = speed[in_trial]\nd0 = d - d.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\ns0 = sp_ - sp_.mean()\ndenom = np.sqrt((d0 ** 2).sum(axis=1) * (s0 ** 2).sum())\nwith np.errstate(invalid=\"ignore\", divide=\"ignore\"):\n    speed_corr = (d0 @ s0) / denom\nspeed_corr = np.nan_to_num(speed_corr, nan=0.0)\nkeep_cells = speed_corr <= SPEED_CORR_THRESH      # SPEED_CORR_THRESH = 0.5\ndff = dff[keep_cells]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 3 quotes the Methods for both rules (\"Manual curation\neliminated ROIs containing multiple somata or dendrites ...\"; \"Additional putative\ninterneurons were detected for exclusion ... by a Pearson correlation of >0.5 between\ntheir dF/F timeseries and the animal's running speed\"). Step 9 checks the exclusion rate\nagainst the paper's \"0.42 ± 0.85% of cells\" (obtained 0.35 ± 0.61%) and the per-session\nneuron count against the paper's \"155–2172 putative pyramidal neurons per session\"\n(obtained min 155 `iscell` / 154 after interneuron removal; the upper bound 2341 is\ninvestigated and attributed to the 3 two-plane m18 sessions). Step 5 decisions 3 and 4\njustify *not* applying the paper's <2 cm/s speed mask (\"speed is a decoder **output**\nwhose class 0 is exactly '< 2 cm/s'\") and *not* restricting to place cells (\"the decoder\nshould see the full curated pyramidal population\").\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Nothing beyond slicing: the alignment event is the trial start, and the neural trace\nis cut at the `trial_start` frame, so sample 0 of every trial *is* the alignment event.\nBehaviour and imaging already live on a single shared frame clock in the NWB (the\nreference `vr_align_to_2P` interpolated VR onto the 2P frame times before export), so the\nsame index window aligns all streams. `off_start = 0.0`, `off_end = None`.\n\nii.\n```python\ns, e = starts[i], ends[i]\nneural_trials.append(np.ascontiguousarray(dff[:, s:e], dtype=np.float32))\ninp[0] = ts[s:e] - ts[s]           # time from trial start (s)\n...\n\"temporal_alignment_event\": (\n    \"trial start = VR 'trial_start' event, i.e. entry onto the linear \"\n    \"track at position 0 cm after the intertrial teleport period\"),\n\"off_start\": 0.0,\n\"off_end\": None,\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 3/Step 10 Check 3: \"VR behaviour is interpolated onto the 2P\nframe times (`vr_align_to_2P`); the NWB already stores it that way (one shared timestamp\nvector)\", so \"the NWB *is* the output of the reference alignment step\". Step 10 Check 2\nverifies per-trial alignment against the raw files (whole-trial `np.allclose` matches,\n`max|diff| = 0`) and Step 7 verifies it visually — \"the blue `trial_start` and red\n`teleport` markers bracket exactly one track traversal\" and \"the input\n`time_from_trial_start_s` starts at 0 for every trial\".\n\n## 2-e. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. The native 2-photon frame period is kept: **64.4836 ms** (15.5078 Hz per imaging\nplane), identical in all 152 sessions. **No rebinning, resampling or interpolation is\napplied at all.** The bin size written to metadata is the median of `np.diff(timestamps)`\ntaken over sessions. For the two-plane animals the stored series `rate` is the 31 Hz\nvolume rate but the per-plane sampling — and therefore the behaviour timestamp spacing —\nis the same 15.5 Hz, so no special handling is needed.\n\nii.\n```python\ninfo[\"dt\"] = float(np.median(np.diff(ts)))\n...\ndt = float(np.median([i[\"dt\"] for i in infos]))\n\"time_bin_size\": dt * 1000.0,\n\"sampling_rate_hz\": 1.0 / dt,\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, decision 1: \"**Time bin = native imaging frame (64.484 ms).**\nEvery one of the 152 sessions has exactly the same `dt` (15.5078 Hz per plane), and the\nNWB behaviour is already interpolated onto that clock by the reference `vr_align_to_2P`.\nUsing the native grid therefore satisfies 'same bin size for all trials and sessions'\nwith **zero resampling**, i.e. no risk of introducing temporal misalignment between the\nneural and behavioural streams.\" Step 9 cross-checks it against the paper's \"0.0645 s\nimaging frame samples\".\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *Time from start of trial in seconds* derived from?\n\ni. The `timestamps` attached to the `position` `BehavioralTimeSeries` (in seconds). What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. Three exclusions, applied to the raw trial list:\n1. **Lick-sensor failure** — the paper's rule implemented literally: a trial is dropped\n   if more than 30% of its imaging frames have a cumulative lick count > 2. This removes\n   exactly **81** trials, the number the paper reports.\n2. **Unscanned trials** — any trial overlapping frames with `scanning < 0` (0 such trials).\n3. **Too-short trials** — fewer than 2 imaging frames (0 such trials).\n12,216 raw → 12,135 kept trials. Note the paper NaNs the lick channel of the 81\nlick-error trials rather than dropping the trials; the AI drops the whole trial because\nNaN is not allowed in the target format.\n\nii.\n```python\nLICK_ERR_COUNT_THRESH = 2      # cumulative lick count per imaging frame\nLICK_ERR_FRAC_THRESH = 0.3     # fraction of frames in the trial\n...\ntrial_lick_error[i] = (np.mean(lick[s:e] > LICK_ERR_COUNT_THRESH)\n                       > LICK_ERR_FRAC_THRESH)\ntrial_unscanned[i] = np.any(scanning[s:e] < 0)\n...\ntrial_len = ends - starts\ntoo_short = trial_len < 2\nkeep_trial = ~(trial_lick_error | trial_unscanned | too_short)\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 3 quotes the Methods: \"A very small number of trials with\nerroneous lick detection ... (~0.65% of all imaged trials, n = 81 out of 12,376 trials)\"\nand the rule \">30% of the 0.0645 s imaging frame samples in the trial containing a\ncumulative lick count >2\". Step 4 records the match as an exact consistency check:\n\"My implementation of the methods rule finds **exactly 81** trials ... Exact match → the\ntrial-curation rule is implemented correctly.\" Step 9 gives the bookkeeping identity\n`raw trials 12,216 = kept 12,135 + lick-error 81 + unscanned 0 + too-short 0`.\n\n## 2-a. What variables in the raw data is the `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. The raw suite2p traces: `ophys/Fluorescence/plane<k>` (`F`) and\n`ophys/Neuropil/plane<k>` (`Fneu`), restricted to the ROIs flagged by\n`ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation/iscell[:,0]`. For the two two-plane animals (m17,\nm18) each plane is a separate `RoiResponseSeries` and the planes are pooled by\nscattering each plane's traces into the rows of the `PlaneSegmentation` table indicated\nby `planeIdx`. The NWB's stored `Deconvolved` array is deliberately **not** used.\n\nii.\n```python\nfluo = ophys.data_interfaces[\"Fluorescence\"].roi_response_series\nneuro = ophys.data_interfaces[\"Neuropil\"].roi_response_series\nplane_keys = sorted(fluo.keys(), key=lambda k: int(k.replace(\"plane\", \"\")))\nF = np.empty((n_roi_total, n_frames), dtype=np.float64)\nFneu = np.empty((n_roi_total, n_frames), dtype=np.float64)\nfor k in plane_keys:\n    p = int(k.replace(\"plane\", \"\"))\n    rows = np.where(plane_idx_all == p)[0]\n    assert len(rows) == fluo[k].data.shape[1], (\n        f\"{k}: {len(rows)} ROIs in table vs {fluo[k].data.shape[1]} traces\")\n    F[rows] = np.asarray(fluo[k].data[:]).T\n    Fneu[rows] = np.asarray(neuro[k].data[:]).T\nplane_idx = plane_idx_all[iscell]\nF = F[iscell]\nFneu = Fneu[iscell]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 2: \"`Deconvolved/plane0` — suite2p `spks` computed from **raw\nF** (values in raw fluorescence units, e.g. 0–3800), *not* the paper's deconvolution of\ndF/F\", so the neural signal has to be recomputed from `F`/`Fneu` either way. Step 5\ndecision 10: the two planes in m17/m18 are deep/superficial CA1 and are \"pooled for all\nanalyses except those in Extended Data Fig. 7\". The `iscell` filter is applied before\nthe dF/F arithmetic as a memory/speed optimisation (every dF/F step is per-cell).\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. dF/F is computed with a port of the reference `reward_relative/preprocessing.py::dff()`\nin the `neuropil_method='subtract'`, `baseline_method='maximin'`, `subtract_baseline=True`,\n`keep_teleports=False` configuration: (1) NaN everything outside `[trial_start, teleport)`;\n(2) `F − 0.7·Fneu`; (3) add the trial-mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F;\n(4) per-trial maximin baseline — NaN-tolerant Gaussian smoothing with σ = 15 samples,\nthen a 300-sample `minimum_filter1d` followed by a 300-sample `maximum_filter1d`\n(300 samples / 15.5 Hz ≈ 19.3 s ≈ the Methods' \"20 s window\"); (5) `dF/F = (F − F0)/|F0|`;\n(6) a 2-sample σ Gaussian smoothing per trial. `nansmooth` is a verbatim port of the\nreference helper. The result is stored as float32.\n\n**The deconvolution step is not applied.** The Methods end the pipeline with \"The\nactivity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using\nthe OASIS algorithm\"; the AI implemented and tested OASIS (in `cache/test_dff.py`,\n`cache/test_dff2.py`) but ships the smoothed dF/F as the `neural` signal. Also,\n`keep_teleports` is hard-coded to `False` for every session; the reference repo sets it\nper animal and per experiment day from `teleport_metadata.py` (the days on which the\nlaser was not blanked between trials), which the AI did not pick up.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_dff(F, Fneu, trial_starts, trial_ends):\n    f_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan); fneu_ = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        f_[:, s:e] = F[:, s:e]; fneu_[:, s:e] = Fneu[:, s:e]\n    in_trial = ~np.isnan(f_[0, :])\n    f_ -= NEU_COEF * fneu_                                   # NEU_COEF = 0.7\n    flow = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        f_[:, s:e] = f_[:, s:e] + NEU_COEF * np.nanmean(fneu_[:, s:e], axis=1, keepdims=True)\n        tmp = nansmooth(f_[:, s:e], BASELINE_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)          # sigma = 15\n        tmp = sp.ndimage.minimum_filter1d(tmp, BASELINE_FILTER_LEN, axis=-1) # 300\n        flow[:, s:e] = sp.ndimage.maximum_filter1d(tmp, BASELINE_FILTER_LEN, axis=-1)\n    dff = np.full(F.shape, np.nan)\n    dff[:, in_trial] = ((f_[:, in_trial] - flow[:, in_trial]) / np.abs(flow[:, in_trial]))\n    for s, e in zip(trial_starts, trial_ends):\n        dff[:, s:e] = nansmooth(dff[:, s:e], DFF_SMOOTH_SIGMA, axis=1)       # sigma = 2\n    return dff, in_trial\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 5, decision 2: \"**Neural signal = dF/F** (computed exactly as\nin `preprocessing.dff`), not the deconvolved trace. Rationale: (a) the NWB's\n`Deconvolved` array is suite2p's spks from *raw* F and does **not** correspond to the\npaper's deconvolution, so it had to be recomputed either way; (b) the paper itself uses\nbinned dF/F for its spatial peak identification 'as this signal is the closest to the raw\ndata'; (c) I tested both signals with a PCA+logistic position decoder on three sessions —\ndF/F was equal or better in every case (m11 d3 0.53 vs 0.45, m19 d6 0.77 vs 0.63, m13 d8\n0.40 vs 0.41), which is expected because the decoder reads instantaneous activity and\ndF/F retains the temporal integration that a sparse event train discards. The\ndeconvolution step itself is implemented and validated but not used.\" Step 10 Check 3\ntabulates the dF/F pipeline against the reference operation-by-operation and reports it\nas matching; the one-frame window difference is argued to be negligible for a 300-sample\nmaximin window. `keep_teleports=False` is justified in Step 1 only by\n`utilities.py::default_dff_method`.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters, both the paper's. (1) ROIs are restricted to suite2p's manual curation,\n`iscell[:,0] == 1`, applied before any dF/F arithmetic. (2) Putative interneurons are\ndropped: cells whose dF/F correlates with the animal's running speed at Pearson\nr > 0.5, computed over all within-trial samples. The correlation is vectorised over all\ncells at once; NaN correlations are mapped to 0 (i.e. kept). 138,678 `iscell` ROIs →\n138,276 neurons after removing 402 putative interneurons (0.29% overall,\n0.35 ± 0.61% per session). No place-cell selection and no speed threshold are applied.\n\nii.\n```python\niscell = np.asarray(plane_seg[\"iscell\"].data)[:, 0].astype(bool)\nF = F[iscell]; Fneu = Fneu[iscell]\n...\nd = dff[:, in_trial]\nsp_ = speed[in_trial]\nd0 = d - d.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\ns0 = sp_ - sp_.mean()\ndenom = np.sqrt((d0 ** 2).sum(axis=1) * (s0 ** 2).sum())\nwith np.errstate(invalid=\"ignore\", divide=\"ignore\"):\n    speed_corr = (d0 @ s0) / denom\nspeed_corr = np.nan_to_num(speed_corr, nan=0.0)\nkeep_cells = speed_corr <= SPEED_CORR_THRESH      # SPEED_CORR_THRESH = 0.5\ndff = dff[keep_cells]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 3 quotes the Methods for both rules (\"Manual curation\neliminated ROIs containing multiple somata or dendrites ...\"; \"Additional putative\ninterneurons were detected for exclusion ... by a Pearson correlation of >0.5 between\ntheir dF/F timeseries and the animal's running speed\"). Step 9 checks the exclusion rate\nagainst the paper's \"0.42 ± 0.85% of cells\" (obtained 0.35 ± 0.61%) and the per-session\nneuron count against the paper's \"155–2172 putative pyramidal neurons per session\"\n(obtained min 155 `iscell` / 154 after interneuron removal; the upper bound 2341 is\ninvestigated and attributed to the 3 two-plane m18 sessions). How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. The native 2-photon frame period is kept: **64.4836 ms** (15.5078 Hz per imaging\nplane), identical in all 152 sessions. **No rebinning, resampling or interpolation is\napplied at all.** The bin size written to metadata is the median of `np.diff(timestamps)`\ntaken over sessions. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. The continuous value itself is not stored.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef discretize_reward_distance(pos, zone_start, zone_end):\n    d = np.zeros_like(pos)\n    before = pos < zone_start\n    after = pos > zone_end\n    d[before] = pos[before] - zone_start\n    d[after] = pos[after] - zone_end\n    ...\n    return out, d\n...\nzs, ze = REWARD_ZONES[zone_labels[i]]\np = pos[s:e]\nout[0], _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, zs, ze)\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES Step 7 verified it graphically: \"The signed reward-zone\ndistance crosses 0 exactly where the position trace enters the shaded reward zone\", and\nStep 10 Check 2 recomputed `output[0]` from the raw position for spot-checked sessions\n(PASS).\n\n## 7-c.
