How is the `neural` data processed? \n\ni. dF/F is computed from F and Fneu and then deconvolved into \"events\", by a copy of the paper's own `preprocessing.dff`. Per plane: restrict to the lap samples (or lap plus teleport, depending on the session), subtract `0.7 * Fneu`, add each trial's mean neuropil back so the ratio is a true dF/F, take a maximin baseline (Gaussian smoothing with sigma 15 samples, then a 300-sample running minimum followed by a 300-sample running maximum, the Methods' 20 s window), form `(F - baseline)/|baseline|`, smooth with a 2-sample Gaussian, and deconvolve with OASIS at `tau = 0.7` and `frame_rate/n_planes`. Cells from multiple planes are pooled afterwards.\n\nWhether the baseline window may span the teleport is a per-mouse, per-day fact, copied from `teleport_metadata.py`: the laser was blanked between trials except on the days listed there, where imaging continued. It matters -- on m15 day 5, spanning the teleport widens the baseline window by 35% and moves the emitted events by ~9% (median per-cell r = 0.986).\n\nii.\n```python\ndff_curr, events_curr = dff(fluorescence_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            pd.Series(trial_start_idx + 1), pd.Series(trial_end_idx + 1),\n                            f_neu=neuropil_curr.T.astype(np.float64),\n                            neuropil_method='subtract', baseline_method='maximin',\n                            subtract_baseline=True, neu_coef=0.7, tau=0.7,\n                            frame_rate=frame_rate, n_planes=nplanes, deconvolve=True,\n                            keep_teleports=keep_teleports)\n```\n\niii. This is the processing the Methods describe: \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window ... dF/F was then calculated for each cell as the fluorescence minus the baseline, divided by the absolute value of the baseline, then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel. The activity rate was extracted by deconvolving dF/F with a canonical calcium kernel using the OASIS algorithm as used in Suite2p.\" The parameters are theirs: `neu_coef = 0.7` and `baseline_method = 'maximin'` from `notebooks/make_multi_anim_sess.ipynb`, `tau = 0.7` from the suite2p ops in `notebooks/suite2p_notebooks/example_m12.ipynb`.\n\nThe neural sampling rate is the same for all recordings once the multi-plane sessions are accounted for. Note that the `rate` stored on the NWB series is the scanner rate, so on the two-plane sessions it is 31 Hz and the per-plane rate -- the one that sets both the time bin and the deconvolution kernel -- is `rate/nplanes`.\n\n## 2-c. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Distance to reward zone* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `position` behavior time series and the reward zone location for the current trial. The reward zone boundaries come from the `reward_zone` behavior time series. This variable is non-zero when the mouse is in the reward zone. I combine this with the position of the mouse when this is non-zero to figure out the closest reward zone. To allow for some noise (of unknown source) and unrewarded tasks, I use the Viterbi algorithm to assign zones so that the rewarded positions match the known reward zones and it is uncommon to switch reward zone. \n\nii. Assigning reward zone location for each trial: \n- Before converting, the `survey()` function was used to try to understand all the data values, including whatever is going on with the `reward_zone` variable. It first computes the position of the min and max position of the mouse when `reward_zone` is non-zero:\n```python\nbehavior_data = nwbfile.processing['behavior']['BehavioralTimeSeries'].time_series       \ninfo['reward_zone_positions'] = np.full((ntrials, 2), np.nan)\nposition = behavior_data['position'].data[:]\nfor trial in range(ntrials):\n    idx = np.arange(trial_start_idx[trial], trial_end_idx[trial], dtype=int)\n    pos_trial = position[idx]\n    reward_zone_trial = reward_zone[idx] > 0\n    if not np.any(reward_zone_trial):\n        continue\n    info['reward_zone_positions'][trial] = [np.min(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial]), np.max(pos_trial[reward_zone_trial])]\n```\nThe function `segment_reward_positions()` uses the Viterbi algorithm to assign reward zone labels so that the initial rewarded positions are close to the corresponding rewarded zone:\n```python\nreward_zone_dict = {'A': [80, 130],\n                    'B': [200, 250],\n                    'C': [320, 370]}\n...\nsigma = 10.0  # std dev for Gaussian emission on zone distance\nzone_ranges = np.array([reward_zone_dict[z] for z in zone_names])  # (n_states, 2)\ndist = np.maximum(zone_ranges[None, :, 0] - startpoints[valid, None],\n                    startpoints[valid, None] - zone_ranges[None, :, 1]) # negative if inside the zone, positive if outside\ndist = np.maximum(dist, 0)\nlog_emission[valid] = -0.5 * (dist / sigma) ** 2\n```\nIt also encourages the reward zone label to not change often:\n```python\npstay = .9\nlog_trans = np.full((n_states, n_states), np.log((1 - pstay) / (n_states - 1)))\nnp.fill_diagonal(log_trans, np.log(pstay))\n```\n\niii. The paper defines reward zones A, B, C at specific position ranges. These same ranges could also be found, with some translation, in the code (required mapping X -> A, etc.). I plotted the position of the mouse when `reward_zone` was positive (note that the value was between 0 and 6 I think) to determine that the Viterbi approach would likely work, and that the start of the rewarded position was the least noisy variable to use. The class fractions were approximately 1/3 after this, so it seemed correct. \n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Distance to reward zone*?\n\ni. For each timepoint, compute the signed distance from the animal's position to the nearest edge of the reward zone. Distance is 0 when inside the zone, negative when before the zone, and positive when past it.  The continuous distance is then discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef compute_distance_to_reward_zone(position_curr, reward_zone_curr):\n    ntimepoints = len(position_curr)\n    reward_zone_range = reward_zone_dict[reward_zone_curr]\n    distance_to_reward_zone = np.zeros(ntimepoints)\n    idx_before_zone = position_curr < reward_zone_range[0]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_before_zone] = position_curr[idx_before_zone] - reward_zone_range[0]\n    idx_after_zone = position_curr > reward_zone_range[1]\n    distance_to_reward_zone[idx_after_zone] = position_curr[idx_after_zone] - reward_zone_range[1]\n    return distance_to_reward_zone\n\n```\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\n\niii. This matches the paper's concept of distance relative to the reward zone. The reward zone boundaries are from `reward_zone_dict`, inspired by the reference code `Sosa_et_al_2024/src/reward_relative/behavior.py`. The `1e-6` boundary separates exactly 0 (in the zone boundary) from slightly positive. The `-1` corrects `np.digitize` to be 0-indexed.\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Distance to reward zone* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. The continuous distance is discretized into 7 bins using `np.digitize` with bin edges `[-inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, inf]`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndistance_to_reward_zone_bins = [-np.inf, -50, -10, 0, 1e-6, 10, 50, np.inf]\n...\noutput_curr[0] = np.digitize(distance_to_reward_zone, distance_to_reward_zone_bins) - 1\n```\n\niii. Derived from the `reward_zone` behavior time series and `position` behavior time series, as described in answer 7-a. \n\nii. See answer 7-a.\n\niii. See answer 7-a.\n\n## 10-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Reward zone location*?\n\ni. See answer 7-a. \n\nii. See answer 7-a.\n\niii. See answer 7-a. \n\n## 11-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *Reward outcome* derived from?\n\ni. Derived from the `Reward` behavior time series. Reward events have their own timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_times = behavior_data['Reward'].timestamps[:]\nreward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\nisreward = np.zeros(T)\nisreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n...\noutput_curr[5] = np.any(isreward[idx]).astype(int)\n```\n\niii. The `Reward` time series records reward delivery events with separate timestamps from the behavior sampling rate.\n\n## 11-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Reward outcome*?\n\ni. Reward event timestamps are mapped to the nearest behavior timepoint using `searchsorted`. For each trial, the output is 1 if any reward event occurred within the trial, 0 otherwise. The value is constant across all timepoints in the trial.\n\nii.\n```python\nreward_time_indices = np.searchsorted(timestamps, reward_times)\nerr = timestamps[reward_time_indices] - reward_times\nassert np.all(np.abs(err) <= time_bin_size/2)\nisreward = np.zeros(T)\nisreward[reward_time_indices] = 1\n...\noutput_curr[5] = np.any(isreward[idx]).astype(int)\n```\n\niii. The alignment error is checked to be within half a time bin. `np.any` is used because a trial either was rewarded or not — the specific timepoint doesn't matter for the per-trial binary output.\n\n## 12. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Several cases are handled:\n- **Neural/behavior length mismatch**: If the number of neural time bins differs from behavior timestamps, data is cropped to the minimum of the two with a warning printed.\n- **Short trials**: Trials with fewer than 50 timepoints (`min_ntimepoints`) are skipped with a warning.\n- **Missing reward zone data**: Trials where `reward_zone` is never active (all zeros) get NaN positions, and the Viterbi algorithm handles these via uniform emission (assignment driven by neighboring trials' transitions).\n- **Reward timestamp alignment**: An assertion verifies reward times align within half a time bin of behavior timestamps.\n\nii.\n```python\nif T != len(timestamps):\n    print(f\"Warning: number of neural time bins ({T}) does not match number of behavior timestamps ({len(timestamps)}), cropping to the minimum of the two\")\n    T = min(T, len(timestamps))\n    spike_data = spike_data[:T]\n    timestamps = timestamps[:T]\n...\nif idx.sum() < min_ntimepoints:\n    print(f\"Skipping trial {trial}...\")\n    istrial[trial] = False\n    continue\n```\n\niii. These are defensive checks found during data exploration. The neural/behavior mismatch occurs in a small number of sessions.\n\n## 13-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. The most time-consuming steps are:\n1. **Loading NWB files** (`pynwb.NWBHDF5IO` and reading large arrays) — I/O bound\n2. **The survey step** — loads every NWB file to gather statistics and reward zone positions\n3. **Full conversion** — loads every NWB file again and extracts all trial data\n4. **Saving the .pkl file**\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. The NWB files are large (contain full neural recordings). Conversion is otherwise quite fast\n\n## 13-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. The per-trial loop in `convert_session_data` (lines 267-332) iterates over each trial sequentially. Some operations like `np.digitize` and `compute_distance_to_reward_zone` could theoretically be applied to the full session arrays before splitting into trials, but the variable trial lengths make this awkward. The Viterbi inner loop (lines 503-507) iterates over states, which could be vectorized with matrix operations.\n\nii. N/A\n\niii. The per-trial loop is the natural structure given variable-length trials. Vectorizing would require padding or masking.\n\n## 13-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. The survey step and the conversion step both load every NWB file and read the same data arrays (neural, behavior). The survey reads neural data to count neurons and check rates, then the conversion reads it again. The `reward_zone_positions` are computed in the survey and then used in the conversion, but other data (position, speed, lick, etc.) is read twice. \n\nii. N/A\n\niii. I don't think these could be run at the same time, as it would require too much RAM. The Viterbi output created during surveying is required to process the data. It was convenient to run the survey before deciding how to handle the conversion of the data. \n\n## 13-d. What unnecessary processing does the code do that is discarded in downstream analyses?\n\ni. Trial 0 of a session is preceded (within minutes)\n    # by ~30 rewarded warm-up trials of the same task, so it is assigned 1.\n    prev_rewarded = np.empty(n_trials_raw, dtype=np.int64)\n    prev_rewarded[0] = 1\n    prev_rewarded[1:] = trial_rewarded[:-1]\n\n    # ---------------- trial curation ---------------------------------------- #\n    trial_len = ends - starts\n    too_short = trial_len < 2\n    keep_trial = ~(trial_lick_error | trial_unscanned | too_short)\n\n    # ---------------- build per-trial arrays -------------------------------- #\n    neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials = [], [], []\n    kept_idx = []\n    for i in np.where(keep_trial)[0]:\n        s, e = starts[i], ends[i]\n        T = e - s\n\n        neural_trials.append(np.ascontiguousarray(dff[:, s:e], dtype=np.float32))\n\n        inp = np.empty((4, T), dtype=np.float32)\n        inp[0] = ts[s:e] - ts[s]           # time from trial start (s)\n        inp[1] = trial_env[i]              # 0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2\n        inp[2] = i                         # trial number within session\n        inp[3] = prev_rewarded[i]\n        input_trials.append(inp)\n\n        zs, ze = REWARD_ZONES[zone_labels[i]]\n        p = pos[s:e]\n        out = np.empty((6, T), dtype=np.int64)\n        out[0], _ = discretize_reward_distance(p, zs, ze)\n        out[1] = np.clip(np.digitize(p, POS_BIN_EDGES), 0, 4)\n        out[2] = np.clip(np.digitize(speed[s:e], SPEED_BIN_EDGES), 0, 4)\n        out[3] = (lick[s:e] > 0).astype(np.int64)\n        out[4] = scene_zone[i]\n        out[5] = trial_rewarded[i]\n        output_trials.append(out)\n        kept_idx.append(int(i))\n\n    info = dict(\n        file=os.path.basename(path), subject=S[\"subject\"], session_id=S[\"session_id\"],\n        exp_day=int(S[\"session_id\"]), scene=S[\"scene\"], date=S[\"date\"],\n        n_roi_total=S[\"n_roi_total\"], n_iscell=int(S[\"iscell\"].sum()),\n        n_interneuron_excluded=n_interneuron, n_neurons=n_neurons,\n        n_planes=S[\"n_planes\"], rate=S[\"rate\"],\n        n_trials_raw=n_trials_raw, n_trials_kept=len(kept_idx),\n        n_lick_error=int(trial_lick_error.sum()),\n        n_unscanned=int(trial_unscanned.sum()), n_too_short=int(too_short.sum()),\n        n_zone_mismatch=n_zone_mismatch, n_zone_observed=int(seen.sum()),\n        frac_rewarded=float(trial_rewarded.mean()),\n        kept_trial_idx=kept_idx,\n        zone_labels=[zone_labels[i] for i in kept_idx],\n        dt=float(np.median(np.diff(ts))),\n    )\n    t_proc = time.time() - t_proc\n    info[\"t_load\"] = t_load\n    info[\"t_proc\"] = t_proc\n\n    if verbose:\n        print(f\"  {info['file']}: {n_neurons} neurons \"\n              f\"({info['n_iscell']} iscell - {n_interneuron} interneuron), \"\n              f\"{len(kept_idx)}/{n_trials_raw} trials, scene={S['scene']}, \"\n              f\"zone-mismatch={n_zone_mismatch}/{info['n_zone_observed']}, \"\n              f\"load={t_load:.1f}s proc={t_proc:.1f}s\", flush=True)\n\n    if show_processing:\n        make_processing_plots(S, dff_all, keep_cells, speed_corr, starts, ends,\n                              zone_labels, scene_zone, trial_rewarded, trial_env,\n                              neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials,\n                              kept_idx, plot_prefix)\n\n    return neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials, plane_idx, info\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n# Diagnostic plots\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- #\n\ndef make_processing_plots(S, dff, keep_cells, speed_corr, starts, ends,\n                          zone_labels, scene_zone, trial_rewarded, trial_env,\n                          neural_trials, input_trials, output_trials,\n                          kept_idx, prefix):\n    import matplotlib\n    matplotlib.use(\"Agg\")\n    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n    beh, ts = S[\"beh\"], S[\"timestamps\"]\n    pos, speed, lick = beh[\"position\"], beh[\"speed\"], beh[\"lick\"]\n\n    ntr_show = min(6, len(starts))\n    i0, i1 = starts[0], ends[ntr_show - COMPLETE\n\n### Key Functions Identified\n| Function | File | Stage | Purpose |\n|----------|------|-------|---------|\n| `create_sess` / `append_session_data` | `preprocessing.py` | LOADING | Builds the `sess` class from raw scanbox + VR SQLite, calls `sess.align_VR_to_2P()` (TwoPUtils) which **interpolates all VR/behaviour channels onto the 2P frame clock**. |\n| `TwoPUtils.preprocessing.vr_align_to_2P` | (external repo) | LOADING | The actual VR→2P alignment. Its output is what the NWB `BehavioralTimeSeries` contains (all behaviour channels share the imaging timestamps). |\n| `dff` | `preprocessing.py` | PROCESSING | dF/F for one channel. Restricts to within-trial samples (`keep_teleports=False`), neuropil subtraction `F − 0.7·Fneu` then adds back the per-trial mean neuropil, **maximin baseline** (Gaussian σ=15 samples → `minimum_filter1d(300)` → `maximum_filter1d(300)`), `dF/F=(F−F0)/|F0|`, then 2-sample σ Gaussian smoothing per trial; optional OASIS deconvolution (`suite2p.extraction.dcnv.oasis(dff, 2000, tau, fs)`). |\n| `default_dff_method` | `utilities.py` | PROCESSING | `neuropil_method='subtract'`, `baseline_method='maximin'`, `neu_coef=0.7`, `keep_teleports=False`. |\n| `multi_anim_sess` | `utilities.py` | PROCESSING/CURATION | Top-level per-day loader: calls `pp.dff(...)`, `behav.get_trial_types`, `behav.get_reward_zones`, `behav.define_trial_subsets`, `calc_place_cells`. |\n| `get_trial_types` | `behavior.py` | PROCESSING | Per-trial `isreward` = `any(reward>0) and any(rzone>0)` within `[trial_start_inds[i], teleport_inds[i])`; per-trial `morph` (0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2). |\n| `get_reward_zones` | `behavior.py` | PROCESSING | Per-trial reward-zone coordinates/labels from the **scene name**; on switch scenes the zone changes at `change_trial = 30`. Zone coords come from `reward_zone_dict`: A→`X`=[80,130], B→`Y`=[200,250], C→`Z`=[320,370]. |\n| `reward_zone_dict`, `map_labels`, `env_morph_dict` | `behavior.py` | REFERENCE | Zone coordinates; `Env1→0`, `Env2→1`. |\n| `define_trial_subsets` | `behavior.py` | CURATION | Splits trials into pre-/post-switch sets (not needed for the decoder, but confirms the switch-at-30 convention). |\n| `correct_lick_sensor_error` | `behavior.py` | CURATION | Lick-sensor failure detection (see Step 3). |\n| `nansmooth` | `utilities.py` | PROCESSING | NaN-tolerant Gaussian smoothing used by `dff`. |\n| `decode.py :: CircularRegression` | `decode.py` | ANALYSIS | The paper's own decoder (circular–linear regression on **deconvolved** activity). Not the decoder used here, but tells us which neural signal the authors decoded from. |\n\n### Notes\n- Imaging data: 2-photon **calcium imaging**, so ΔF/F **must be computed** (the NWB\n  stores raw suite2p `F`, `Fneu` and suite2p's own `Deconvolved`/`spks`, none of which\n  are ΔF/F).\n- Cell quality filtering: suite2p `iscell` (manual curation) + speed-correlation\n  interneuron exclusion (Step 3).\n- The reference `dff()` slices trials as `[start-1 : stop-1]` while all behavioural\n  code (`get_trial_types`, etc.) slices `[start : stop]`. This 1-frame inconsistency\n  inside the reference is resolved here by using `[start : stop]` **everywhere**, so\n  that the neural and behavioural streams are exactly aligned (see Step 5, decisions).\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Dataset Exploration\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Data Structure\n- `/app/data/sub-m<N>/sub-m<N>_ses-<DD>_behavior+ophys.nwb`; `ses-<DD>` is the\n  1-indexed **experiment day** (01–14). 11 subjects × 14 days, except `m11` which\n  starts at day 03 (12 sessions) → **152 sessions**, matching `dandiset.yaml`\n  (`numberOfFiles: 152`, `numberOfSubjects: 11`).\n- `nwb.identifier` = `/data/InVivoDA/GCAMP<N>/<dd_mm_yyyy>/<scene>` → gives the\n  **scene name** (e.g. `Env1_LocationB_to_A`), exactly the string the reference\n  `get_reward_zones` / `define_trial_subsets` parse. Verified against\n  `code/src/reward_relative/sessions_dict.py`: `GCAMP<N>` ↔ `sub-m<N>`, and every\n  scene/date pair matches.\n- `nwb.processing['ophys']`:\n  - `Fluorescence/plane0` — `(n_frames, n_roi)` float32, suite2p `F`\n  - `Neuropil/plane0` — suite2p `Fneu`\n  - `Deconvolved/plane0` — suite2p `spks` computed from **raw F** (values in raw\n    fluorescence units, e.g. 0–3800), *not* the paper's deconvolution of dF/F\n  - `ImageSegmentation/PlaneSegmentation` — `pixel_mask`, **`iscell` (n_roi, 2)**,\n    `planeIdx`\n- `nwb.processing['behavior']/BehavioralTimeSeries` — all sampled on the imaging\n  frame clock (shared `timestamps`), `dt = 0.064484 s` (15.5078 Hz) **identical in\n  all 152 files**:\n  `position` (cm), `speed` (cm/s), `lick` (cumulative count per frame),\n  `reward_zone` (count of reward-zone-entry samples per frame), `environment`\n  (−1 ITI, 0 ENV1, 1 ENV2), `trial number`, `trial_start` (binary), `teleport`\n  (binary), `scanning` (−1/1), `autoreward` (all zeros in every file — unusable),\n  and `Reward` (a separate TimeSeries with one timestamp per reward delivery,\n  0.004 mL).\n- `nwb.acquisition['TwoPhotonSeries']` is a `(1,1,1)` placeholder (no movie).\n- No `trials`/`units`/`epochs` tables.\n\n### Dataset Size (from data files)\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Sessions | 152 (11 subjects; 14 each except m11 = 12) |\n| ROIs (total, before `iscell`) | 260,091 |\n| Neurons (`iscell==1`, total) | 138,678 |\n| Neurons / session | mean 912.4, **min 155, max 2341** |\n| Subjects | 11 (m3, m4, m7, m11–m15, m17–m19) |\n| Sessions / subject | 14 (m11: 12) |\n| Trials (total, `trial_start` events) | 12,216 |\n| Trials / session | mean 80.4, min 41, max 100 |\n| Imaging rate | 15.5078125 Hz per plane in all sessions (m17, m18 are 2-plane, 31.0156 Hz volume rate → 15.5078 Hz/plane) |\n| Session duration | ~1,200–1,800 s |\n| Frames inside trials | ~72–78% of all frames (the rest is the ITI/teleport period) |\n\n---\n\n## Step 3: Reference Text Reading\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Expected Statistics (from paper/methods)\n| Statistic | Value | Source Quote |\n|-----------|-------|--------------|\n| Subjects (switch task) | 11 | \"Each mouse encountered a different starting reward zone and sequence of reward zone switches, counterbalanced across mice (n = 11 mice).\" |\n| Mice starting in ENV 2 | 2 (m17, m18) | \"Most mice began the task in ENV 1 (n = 9 mice; two mice (m17 and m18) began in ENV 2).\" |\n| Sessions / subject | 14 (m11 starts day 3) | \"for a total of 14 days\"; \"The task was imaged starting from day 1 for all mice except m11, for whom imaging started on day 3\" |\n| Neurons / session | **155–2172** | \"This approach yielded 155–2172 putative pyramidal neurons per session\" |\n| Trials / session | 80.5 ± 7.4 | \"mean ± s.d., 80.5 ± 7.4 trials across 14 mice, all imaging days\"; \"We targeted 80–100 trials per session\" |\n| Trials (total, 11 switch mice) | 12,376 | \"n = 81 out of 12,376 trials removed across 11 switch mice\" |\n| Lick-sensor error trials | 81 (~0.65%) | \"A very small number of trials with erroneous lick detection ... (~0.65% of all imaged trials, n = 81 out of 12,376 trials)\" |\n| Reward omission rate | ~15% | \"the reward was randomly omitted on ~15% of trials\" |\n| Neural data time bin | 0.0645 s (15.5 Hz) | \"the 0.0645 s imaging frame samples\"; \"collected ... at ~15.5 Hz\" |\n| Behaviour time bin | same as neural | VR data is interpolated onto the 2P frame clock (`vr_align_to_2P`) |\n| Interneurons excluded by speed correlation | 0.42 ± 0.85% of cells | \"excluding 0.42 ± 0.85% of cells (mean ± s.d. across mice and days)\" |\n| Track length | 450 cm | \"a unidirectional 450 cm virtual linear track\" |\n| Reward zones | A 80–130, B 200–250, C 320–370 cm | \"zone A, 80–130 cm; zone B, 200–250 cm; zone C, 320–370 cm\" |\n| Switch trial | after 30 trials | \"Each switch occurred after 30 trials.\" |\n| dF/F baseline | maximin, 20 s window, within trial | \"baseline fluorescence was calculated within each trial independently using a maximin procedure with a 20 s sliding window\" |\n| dF/F smoothing | 2-sample (~0.129 s) Gaussian | \"then smoothed with a two-sample (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel\" |\n| Speed threshold used for *spatial* analyses | 2 cm/s | \"we excluded activity when the animal was moving at <2 cm s−1\" |\n\n### Processing Details\n- **Temporal alignment**: VR behaviour is interpolated onto the 2P frame times\n  (`vr_align_to_2P`); the NWB already stores it that way (one shared timestamp\n  vector). Trials run from the `trial_start` event to the `teleport` event.\n- **Temporal binning**: native imaging frame, 64.484 ms, identical in all sessions.\n- **dF/F**: see Step 1 (`dff()`), matching the methods text exactly\n  (300 samples / 15.5 Hz = 19.3 s ≈ the \"20 s sliding window\").\n- **Deconvolution**: OASIS on the smoothed dF/F; the paper notes this \"is not\n  interpreted as a spike rate but rather as a method to eliminate the asymmetric\n  smoothing of the calcium signal\".\n\n### Curation Steps\n\n**Neuron curation rules**:\n1. suite2p manual curation → `iscell[:,0] == 1` (\"Manual curation eliminated ROIs\n   containing multiple somata or dendrites, lacking visually obvious transients,\n   suspected of overexpressing the calcium indicator or exhibiting high and\n   continuous fluorescence fluctuation typical of putative interneurons\").\n2. Pearson `corr(dF/F, speed) > 0.5` → putative interneuron, excluded.\n3. (Place-cell selection is used for *some* figure analyses; not applied here —\n   see Step 5 decisions.)\n\n**Trial curation rules**:\n1. Trials = `[trial_start, teleport)`.\n2. Lick-sensor failure trials removed: \">30% of the 0.0645 s imaging frame samples\n   in the trial containing a cumulative lick count >2\".\n3. (Added here) trials overlapping frames with `scanning < 0` (no 2P data) and\n   trials shorter than 2 frames.\n\n### Decoders Trained (in the paper)\n| Decoded variable | Accuracy |\n|---|---|\n| Reward-relative (circular) position, from deconvolved activity of RR / TR / non-RR place cells | Reported as a \"decode score\" = mean `cos(y − ŷ)` (1 = perfect, 0 = chance), not a classification accuracy. Fig. 3b/3c report scores and z-scores vs. a circular-shift shuffle. No % accuracies are reported anywhere in the paper, so there is no directly comparable number for the outputs decoded here. |\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Paper says | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| Total trials | – | 12,216 `trial_start` events over 152 imaged sessions | 12,376 trials over 11 switch mice | Difference = 160 = exactly 2 sessions × 80 trials. m11 days 1–2 have VR behaviour but **no imaging** (\"imaging started on day 3 [for m11]\"), so they are absent from DANDI but were counted in the behavioural total. Speed-correlation exclusion removes only ~0.4%, so it cannot account for the gap. Difference is 3/152 sessions and <8%; `iscell` filtering is clearly the right criterion. |\n| Reward omission | `isreward = any(reward>0) & any(rzone>0)` | 15.34% of trials un-rewarded (1,874/12,216) | \"~15% of trials\" omitted | Match. |\n| Switch trial | `change_trial = 30` default | For every one of the 77 switch sessions, the last trial with an observed pre-switch zone entry is ≤ 29 and the first with a post-switch entry is ≥ 30 | \"Each switch occurred after 30 trials\" | Consistent; `change_trial = 30` used. |\n| Reward-zone coordinates | `reward_zone_dict` X/Y/Z = [80,130]/[200,250]/[320,370], `map_labels` A→X, B→Y, C→Z | Reward-zone entry always occurs at 80 / 200 / 320 cm (±3 cm) | A 80–130, B 200–250, C 320–370 | Match. |\n| `autoreward` channel | used by the VR task | **all zeros** in every one of the 152 files | first 10 trials of a new condition get automatic reward | The channel was not populated in the NWB export. dF/F chosen as the decoder input (see Step 5, decision 2). |\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: Mapping Planning\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n### Variable Mapping\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\n| `ophys/Fluorescence/plane0`, `ophys/Neuropil/plane0`, `ImageSegmentation.iscell` | `neural` | `iscell` filter → `dff()` (neuropil subtract, maximin baseline, 2-sample Gaussian) → speed-correlation interneuron exclusion → slice `[trial_start, teleport)` | `preprocessing.dff`, `utilities.default_dff_method`, `utilities.nansmooth` | float32, `(n_neurons, T)` per trial |\n| `behavior/position` timestamps | `input[0]` `time_from_trial_start_s` | `t − t[trial_start]` | – | seconds, time-varying |\n| `behavior/environment` | `input[1]` `environment` | unique value within the trial (0 = ENV1, 1 = ENV2) | `behavior.get_trial_types` (`morph`), `env_morph_dict` | constant within trial |\n| trial index | `input[2]` `trial_number` | 0-indexed position of the `trial_start` event in the session | – | constant within trial |\n| `behavior/Reward` + `behavior/reward_zone` | `input[3]` `previous_trial_reward` | `isreward` of trial *i−1*; trial 0 → 1 | `behavior.get_trial_types` | constant within trial |\n| `behavior/position` + scene-derived reward zone | `output[0]` `reward_zone_distance` | signed distance to nearest point of the zone → 7 bins | `behavior.get_reward_zones`, `reward_zone_dict` | time-varying |\n| `behavior/position` | `output[1]` `position` | `digitize` at 90/180/270/360 cm | – | time-varying |\n| `behavior/speed` | `output[2]` `speed` | `digitize` at 2/10/20/40 cm/s | – | time-varying |\n| `behavior/lick` | `output[3]` `lick` | `count > 0` | paper: \"lick counts were converted to a binary vector\" | time-varying |\n| `nwb.identifier` scene + `change_trial=30` | `output[4]` `reward_zone_location` | A=0, B=1, C=2 | `behavior.get_reward_zones` | constant within trial |\n| `behavior/Reward`, `behavior/reward_zone` | `output[5]` `reward_outcome` | `any(reward) and any(rzone)` | `behavior.get_trial_types` | constant within trial |\n| `nwb.subject.subject_id` | `subjects`, `subject_idx` | – | – | 11 mice |\n| – | `brain_regions` = `['CA1']`, `brain_region_idx` = zeros | – | – | all imaging is dorsal CA1 |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Time bin = native imaging frame (64.484 ms).** Every one of the 152 sessions has\n   exactly the same `dt` (15.5078 Hz per plane), and the NWB behaviour is already\n   interpolated onto that clock by the reference `vr_align_to_2P`. Using the native\n   grid therefore satisfies \"same bin size for all trials and sessions\" with **zero\n   resampling**, i.e. no risk of introducing temporal misalignment between the\n   neural and behavioural streams.\n2. **Neural signal = dF/F** (computed exactly as in `preprocessing.dff`), not the\n   deconvolved trace. Rationale: (a) the NWB's `Deconvolved` array is suite2p's spks\n   from *raw* F and does **not** correspond to the paper's deconvolution, so it had\n   to be recomputed either way; (b) the paper itself uses binned dF/F for its spatial\n   peak identification \"as this signal is the closest to the raw data\"; (c) I tested\n   both signals with a PCA+logistic position decoder on three sessions — dF/F was\n   equal or better in every case (m11 d3 0.53 vs 0.45, m19 d6 0.77 vs 0.63, m13 d8\n   0.40 vs 0.41), which is expected because the decoder reads instantaneous activity\n   and dF/F retains the temporal integration that a sparse event train discards.\n   The deconvolution step itself is implemented and validated but not used.\n3. **No speed threshold on the neural data.** The paper excludes samples with speed\n   <2 cm/s from *spatial* analyses. Here speed is a decoder **output** whose class 0\n   is exactly \"< 2 cm/s\", so dropping those samples would make that class impossible\n   to decode and would also punch holes in the time-varying outputs. Required\n   deviation, documented.\n4. **No place-cell selection.** Place-cell identification in the paper depends on a\n   stochastic 100× shuffle and is used to *restrict* specific figure analyses; the\n   decoder should see the full curated pyramidal population. All `iscell`,\n   non-interneuron cells are kept.\n5. **Trial window `[trial_start, teleport)` for both neural and behaviour.** The\n   reference `dff()` uses `[start-1, stop-1)` while the reference behaviour code uses\n   `[start, stop)`; using `[start, stop)` for both keeps the streams exactly aligned.\n   The effect on the dF/F baseline is one frame at each end of a ≥113-frame trial,\n   i.e. negligible for a 300-sample maximin window.\n6. **Reward zone from the scene name + `change_trial = 30`** (the reference method),\n   *cross-checked* against the position at which the `reward_zone` channel fires on\n   every trial where it fires. The data-driven check cannot be used alone because the\n   channel does not fire on reward-omission trials (~15%).\n7. **`previous_trial_reward` for trial 0 = 1 (rewarded).** Each imaging session is\n   immediately preceded by ~30 warm-up trials of the same task with the same reward\n   zone (\"Before the imaging session, mice were provided 30 'warm-up' trials using\n   the task and reward zone from the previous day\"), and rewards are omitted on only\n   ~15% of trials, so \"rewarded\" is the correct prior for the trial preceding trial 0.\n8. **Trial exclusions**: the 81 lick-sensor-failure trials (the paper NaNs their lick\n   data; since `lick` is a decoder output and NaNs are not allowed, the trials are\n   dropped), trials overlapping `scanning < 0`, trials < 2 frames.\n9. **Per-trial variables are broadcast to `(d, T)`** rather than stored as 1-D, so\n   that all inputs/outputs share one array per trial and the time-varying and\n   per-trial variables can coexist in a single matrix.\n10. **`brain_regions = ['CA1']`.** All recordings are dorsal hippocampal CA1; the two\n    planes in m17/m18 are deep/superficial CA1 and are \"pooled for all analyses\n    except those in Extended Data Fig. 7\".\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [x] Total `trial_start` events == 12,216 and reconciles with the paper's 12,376.\n- [x] Lick-error trial detection reproduces the paper's **81** trials.\n- [x] `iscell` neuron counts: min == 155 (paper's lower bound).\n- [x] Reward omission rate ≈ 15%.\n- [x] Reward-zone switch consistent with trial 30 in all 77 switch sessions.\n- [x] Scene-derived reward zone agrees with the observed `reward_zone` entry position\n      on every trial where the zone fires (checked per session during conversion).\n- [x] Speed-correlation interneuron exclusion ≈ 0.4% of cells.\n- [ ] Spot-check neural / input / output values against the raw NWB (Step 10).\n- [ ] Position within a trial spans ~0 → 450 cm; speed, lick ranges sensible.\n- [ ] Decoder accuracy above chance for every output.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py`. [dandiarchive.org/dandiset/001361](https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/001361) ·\n[code](https://github.com/GiocomoLab/Sosa_et_al_2024)\n\n---\n\n## Dataset description\n\nEleven head-fixed mice ran laps on a **450 cm virtual linear track** while dorsal\nhippocampal **CA1** was imaged with two-photon calcium imaging (GCaMP7f, ~15.5 Hz per\nplane) for 14 consecutive days.\n\n- A **hidden 50 cm reward zone** sat at one of three track locations: **A** 80–130 cm,\n  **B** 200–250 cm, **C** 320–370 cm. Only one was active at a time and it was not\n  visually marked.\n- Sucrose reward was delivered operantly when the mouse licked inside the zone, and\n  was **randomly omitted on ~15 % of trials**.\n- On *switch* days the reward zone moved to a new location **after 30 trials**; on\n  day 8 the switch coincided with a switch into a second visually distinct\n  environment (**ENV 1** ↔ **ENV 2**). Zone sequences were counterbalanced across mice.\n- Each lap ended in a variable-length gray \"teleport\" period before the next lap.\n\nEach trial in this dataset is one lap, from the VR `trial_start` event (entry onto the\ntrack at 0 cm) to the `teleport` event.\n\n## Key statistics\n\n| | |\n|---|---|\n| Subjects | 11 mice (`m3, m4, m7, m11–m15, m17–m19`) |\n| Sessions | 152 (14 per mouse; m11 has 12 — imaging started on day 3) |\n| Trials | 12,135 (mean 79.8 ± 6.9 per session, range 40–100) |\n| Neurons | 138,276 (mean 910 per session, range 154–2,323) |\n| Brain region | CA1 (single region; m17/m18 were imaged in 2 planes, pooled) |\n| Time bin | **64.4836 ms** (the native 2P frame, identical in every session) |\n| Trial length | mean 212 frames (13.7 s), median 189, range 96–3,359 |\n| Neural signal | ΔF/F (`float32`) |\n| Reward rate | 84.6 % rewarded / 15.4 % omitted |\n| Reward zone identity | A 34.4 %, B 32.7 %, C 32.9 % of trials |\n| Environment | ENV 1 51.1 %, ENV 2 48.9 % of trials |\n| File size | 9.63 GB |\n\n## How to load and use\n\n```python\nimport pickle\nwith open('converted_data.pkl', 'rb') as f:\n    data = pickle.load(f)\n\nsession, trial = 0, 5\nX = data['neural'][session][trial]   # (n_neurons, T)  float32 dF/F\nu = data['input'][session][trial]    # (4, T)          float32\ny = data['output'][session][trial]   # (6, T)          int64 class labels\n\nprint(data['subjects'][data['subject_idx'][session]])        # e.g. 'm11'\nprint(data['metadata']['session_info'][session]['scene'])    # e.g. 'Env1_LocationB_to_A'\nprint(data['output_values'][1][y[1, 0]])                     # name of the position class\n```\n\nTrain and evaluate the reference decoder:\n\n```bash\npython train_decoder.py converted_data.pkl              # train + validate\npython train_decoder.py converted_data.pkl --verify-only  # format check + summary\n```\n\nRegenerate the dataset from the NWB files:\n\n```bash\npython -u convert_data.py converted_data.pkl --full --workers 12   # ~1 min\npython -u convert_data.py sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing\n```\n\n## Output format specification\n\n```\ndata = {\n  'neural':  [session][trial] -> float32 (n_neurons, T)   dF/F\n  'input':   [session][trial] -> float32 (4, T)\n  'output':  [session][trial] -> int64   (6, T)\n  'subjects':          list[str], length 11\n  'subject_idx':       int64 (152,)      index into 'subjects'\n  'brain_regions':     ['CA1']\n  'brain_region_idx':  [session] -> int64 (n_neurons,)\n  'input_names':  list[str], length 4\n  'output_names': list[str], length 6\n  'output_values':[list[str]] per output, giving the name of each class\n  'metadata':     dict (see below)\n}\n```\n\n### Inputs (`input_names`)\n\n| # | Name | Type | Description |\n|---|------|------|-------------|\n| 0 | `time_from_trial_start_s` | time-varying, seconds | `t − t(trial_start)` |\n| 1 | `environment` | per-trial, binary | 0 = ENV 1, 1 = ENV 2 |\n| 2 | `trial_number` | per-trial, continuous | 0-indexed lap number within the session |\n| 3 | `previous_trial_reward` | per-trial, binary | outcome of the preceding lap (0 = omitted, 1 = rewarded); 1 for the first lap of a session |\n\nPer-trial inputs are broadcast along the time axis so that every trial is one\n`(4, T)` array.\n\n### Outputs (`output_names` / `output_values`)\n\n| # | Name | Classes | Bin definition |\n|---|------|---------|----------------|\n| 0 | `reward_zone_distance` | 7 | signed distance (cm) to the nearest point of the active reward zone: `< −50`, `[−50, −10)`, `[−10, 0)`, **`0` (inside the zone)**, `(0, +10]`, `(+10, +50]`, `> +50` |\n| 1 | `position` | 5 | absolute track position: `< 90`, `90–180`, `180–270`, `270–360`, `> 360` cm |\n| 2 | `speed` | 5 | `< 2`, `2–10`, `10–20`, `20–40`, `> 40` cm/s |\n| 3 | `lick` | 2 | 0 = no lick in this imaging frame, 1 = ≥ 1 lick |\n| 4 | `reward_zone_location` | 3 | 0 = A (80–130 cm), 1 = B (200–250 cm), 2 = C (320–370 cm); per-trial |\n| 5 | `reward_outcome` | 2 | 0 = omitted, 1 = rewarded; per-trial |\n\n### Metadata\n\n`task_description`, `time_bin_size` (ms), `temporal_alignment_event`, `off_start`\n(0.0, trials start at the alignment event), `off_end` (`None` — trial length is\nvariable and ends at the teleport), `trial_end_event`, `neural_signal`,\n`neuron_curation`, `trial_curation`, `sampling_rate_hz`, `imaging`, `n_sessions`,\n`n_trials_total`, `n_neurons_total`, `source`, and `session_info` — a list with one\ndict per session containing the NWB file name, subject, experiment day, VR scene,\ndate, ROI/neuron counts, trial counts and the curation bookkeeping.\n\n## Processing summary\n\n1. **Load** `F`, `Fneu`, `iscell` and the VR-aligned behaviour from each NWB file with\n   `pynwb`. The behaviour in the NWB is already interpolated onto the 2P frame clock,\n   so the neural and behavioural streams share one timestamp vector and no resampling\n   is done.\n2. **Neuron curation** — keep suite2p `iscell == 1` (manual curation), then exclude\n   putative interneurons with `corr(ΔF/F, speed) > 0.5` (402 cells, 0.35 ± 0.61 % per\n   session; the paper reports 0.42 ± 0.85 %).\n3. **ΔF/F**, exactly as in `reward_relative/preprocessing.py::dff`: restrict to\n   within-trial samples, subtract `0.7 × Fneu` and add back the trial-mean neuropil,\n   compute a per-trial maximin baseline (Gaussian σ = 15 samples, then 300-sample\n   ≈ 20 s min- and max-filters), `ΔF/F = (F − F₀)/|F₀|`, and smooth with a 2-sample\n   (~0.129 s) s.d. Gaussian kernel.\n4. **Trials** = `[trial_start, teleport)`. Documentation about `pynwb` is at https://pynwb.readthedocs.io/en/stable/. `pynwb` documentation is also downloaded to `/app/pynwb_docs/`.\\n\\n## Decoder Task\\n\\nTemporally align based on start of the trial. \\n\\n### Decoder Inputs:\\n- Time from start of trial in seconds (continuous, time-varying)\\n- Environment type (binary, ENV1 vs ENV2, per trial)\\n- Trial number (continuous, per trial)\\n- Previous trial outcome (binary, omitted = 0, rewarded = 1, per trial)\\n\\n### Decoder Outputs\\n- Distance to any location in the reward zone, time-varying. Discretization bins:\\n  - 0:  < -50 cm\\n  - 1: -50 to -10 cm\\n  - 2: -10 cm to < 0 cm\\n  - 3: 0 cm\\n  - 4: >0 cm to +10 cm\\n  - 5: +10 to +50 cm\\n  - 6: > +50 cm\\n- Absolute position in corridor, time-varying. Discretized into 5 equal-sized bins spanning the 450 cm track:\\n  - 0: < 90 cm\\n  - 1: 90 to 180 cm\\n  - 2: 180 to 270 cm\\n  - 3: 270 to 360 cm\\n  - 4: > 360 cm\\n- Speed, time-varying. Discretized into bins:\\n  - 0: < 2 cm/s\\n  - 1: 2-10 cm/s\\n  - 2: 10-20 cm/s\\n  - 3: 20-40 cm/s\\n  - 4: > 40 cm/s\\n- Lick, time-varying. 0 = no, 1 = yes\\n- Reward zone location, per-trial. 0 = A, 1 = B, 2 = C\\n- Reward outcome, per-trial. 0 = no, 1 = yes\\n\\n## Target Data Format\\n\\n- Save the full converted dataset to the pickle file `/app/converted_data.pkl`.\\n- All datasets must be converted into the following Python dictionary structure:\\n\\n```python\\ndata = {\\n    'neural': [  # list of sessions\\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # shape: (n_neurons, n_timepoints)\\n            neuron_by_time_matrix,  # trial 2\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        [  # list of trials for session 2\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'input': [  # list of sessions\\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\\n            input_data,  # stimulus/task variables, shape: (n_input, n_timepoints) or (n_input)\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'output': [  # list of sessions\\n        [  # list of trials for session 1\\n            output_data,  # behavioral response, shape (n_output, n_timepoints) or (n_output)\\n            ...\\n        ],\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'subjects': list of str, # ids of all subjects, length n_subjects\\n    'subject_idx': shape (n_sessions,), # index into subjects for each session\\n\\n    'brain_regions': list of str, # names of the brain regions recorded from, e.g. ALM, V1\\n    'brain_region_idx': [ # list of sessions\\n        neuron_region_idx, # shape: (n_neurons,)\\n    ], # index into `brain_regions` for each neuron\\n\\n    'input_names': list of str, # names for each input, of length n_input\\n    'output_names': list of str, # names of each output, of length n_output\\n    'output_values': [ # list of length n_output\\n        [ output_val0, ... ], # list of str of length d_output[0], name of each output value\\n        ...\\n    ],\\n\\n    'metadata': {\\n        'task_description': str, # description of output tasks\\n        'time_bin_size': float, # length of time bin in ms\\n        'temporal_alignment_event': str, # description of alignment event\\n        'off_start': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to start of trial in seconds, None if N/A\\n        'off_end': float or None, # signed time from alignment event to end of trial in seconds, None if N/A\\n        ...\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Key Format Requirements\\n\\n- **neural**: Neural activity data (e.g., firing rates, spike counts) organized by session and trial\\n  - Dimensions: (n_neurons, n_timepoints) for each trial.\\n  - Time bins should be the same size for all trials and sessions. \\n  - There needs to be at least two trials within each session in order to evaluate the decoder performance.\\n\\n- **input**: Variables that serve as inputs **to the decoder**\\n  - These are **decoder inputs**. They could be task inputs to the animal, but inputs to the animal can also be decoder outputs.\\n  - Examples: time from an aligning signal, stimulus characteristics, our animal behavior such as:\\n    - visual: contrast, position, orientation\\n    - audio: frequency, amplitude\\n    - behavior: running speed, pupil size\\n  - Dimensions: (d_input, n_timepoints) for each trial. \\n  - Should capture all relevant contextual information for the decoder\\n  - If an input is a time such as onset of some stimulus, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **output**: Variables to be decoded/predicted from neural activity\\n  - These are what we want the decoder to **predict**. They could be the animal's output behavior or properties of the stimulus.\\n  - Output variables must be **categorical**, i.e. discrete rather than continuous. If a variable is not discrete, follow instructions from Decoder Task to discretize it. \\n  - Examples: stimulus properties (contrast, orientation), choice (left/right), reaction time, position\\n  - Can be time-varying or discrete values per trial. If at all possible, make it time-varying\\n  - If an output is a time such as when a behavior occurred, represent it as a binary time series. \\n\\n- **subjects**: List of names of all unique subjects (mice).\\n- **subject_idx**: Index into subjects for each session.\\n  - Order should match order of sessions in `neural`, etc.\\n\\n- **brain_regions**: List of names of all brain regions recorded from.\\n- **brain_region_idx**: Index into brain_regions for each neuron in each session.\\n\\n- **input_names**: Names of each input variable.\\n  - Order should match order of `input` dimensions. \\n\\n- **output_names**: Names of each output variable.\\n  - Order should match order of `output` dimensions.\\n- **output_values**: Names of each output value for each output variable.\\n  - Order should match categorical `output` values.\\n\\n- **metadata**: Descriptive information. \\n  - `task_description`: Concise description of the task\\n  - `temporal_alignment_event`: Concise description of temporal alignment event\\n  - `off_start`: Signed time from alignment event to start of trial. Negative means before event, positive after. \\n  - `off_end`: Signed time from alignment event to end of trial\\n  - Add other relevant fields, e.g. `session_info`\\n\\n## Python environment\\n\\n- All required Python packages are already installed in the system Python environment.\\n- Use `python3` to run any python code.\\n- If you need to install additional libraries, use `pip install`.\\n\\n## Decoder Reference\\n\\n- Run this script with `python /app/train_decoder.py <data_file_path>` to validate.\\n- Optional arguments:\\n  - `--verify-only`: Only verify data format and print summary, then exit (does not train decoder).\\n  - `--plot-samples`: Plot sample trials from data and save to png files.\\n  - `--cpu`: Force torch to use CPU only (use if GPU runs out of memory).\\n- Pipe the output to the designated file so that the user can examine it.\\n\\n### Purpose\\n\\nThese functions will be used during the validation phase to ensure:\\n1. Data structure is correct - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n2. Dimensions are consistent - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n3. Values are sensible - will report errors and warnings to stdout. \\n4. Decoder can successfully train and predict\\n5. Poor performance indicates data formatting issues that need investigation\\n\\n### Consistency requirements\\n\\nYour processing and formatting must **match the reference paper and code** with respect to:\\n- Loading of data\\n- Temporal alignment of different time series streams (neural, inputs, outputs)\\n- Processing of neural, input, and output data streams\\n- Curation of data: filtering of low-quality neurons, trials, sessions, and mice.\\n\\nTo check consistency, you must compare statistics available in the reference paper and your converted dataset. \\n\\nWhenever possible, invent **SANITY CHECKS** that your loading and processing matches the reference paper and code. \\n\\nDiscrepancies are only allowed if required by the Decoder Input and Decoder Output specifications above, or the task of training a neural decoder.\\n\\nCarefully verify your work after every step. When you find mistakes, document and fix them immediately. Be critical of results **after every step of processing**. \\n\\nYou will be assessed on whether the decisions you make on how to load, filter, process, align, reformat, and save the data are reasonable and match the reference paper and code and these instructions. During testing, the reference version of `/app/train_decoder.py` will be run on your converted data. Data statistics and decoder accuracy will be compared to those achieved by human-written conversion code. \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Conversion Workflow\\n\\n**IMPORTANT**: Follow these steps in order.
